嘉靖十七年進士登科錄

玉音

嘉靖十七年三月初九日，禮部尚書兼翰林院學士臣嚴嵩等於奉天門奏為科舉事：「會試天下舉人，取中三百二十名。本年三月十五日殿試，合擬讀卷官及執事等官，少傅兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士李時等六十四員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

光祿大夫、柱國、少傅兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士李時，壬戌進士。
光祿大夫、柱國、少傅兼太子太師、禮部尚書、武英殿大學士夏言，丁丑進士。
榮祿大夫、太子太保、吏部尚書許讚，丙辰進士。
translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Seventeenth Year of Jiajing (1538)

The Imperial Voice

On the ninth day of the third month of the seventeenth year of Jiajing, your servant Yan Song, Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Academician of the Hanlin Academy, and others submitted the following memorial at Fengtian Gate concerning the civil-service examinations:

“The Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates from throughout the realm has selected 320 successful candidates. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year, we hereby nominate sixty-four officials as Readers and other functionaries, including Li Shi, Junior Mentor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. The classes and ranks of their metropolitan graduate status shall respectfully follow the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao. The first class shall, according to precedent, comprise three men: the first shall receive secondary sixth rank, and the second and third primary seventh rank, with all three granted the distinction ‘metropolitan graduate with honors.’ Those in the second class shall receive secondary seventh rank and be granted ‘metropolitan graduate status.’ Those in the third class shall receive primary eighth rank and be granted ‘status equivalent to metropolitan graduate.’”

The imperial edict was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Readers

Li Shi, Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall, was a metropolitan graduate of the renxu year.

Xia Yan, Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall, was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.

Xu Zan, Grand Master for Glorious Service, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel, was a metropolitan graduate of the bingchen year.

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month in the seventeenth year of Jiajing (1538), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the nineteenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court dress. That day, the Embroidered-uniform Guard arranged the ceremonial regalia along the palace steps and within the courtyard. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow results proclamation, led by drums and music, out through Chang’an Left Gate. After it had been posted outside the gate, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

On the twentieth day of the third month…

translation_en:
A banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates proceeded to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the rites.
On the twenty-second day of the third month, court robes, a cap, and a belt were bestowed upon the top-ranking graduate (zhuangyuan), and paper currency upon the metropolitan graduates (jinshi).
On the twenty-third day of the third month, the top-ranking graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial of thanks for imperial grace.
On the twenty-fourth day of the third month, the top-ranking graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite.
The Ministry of Rites memorialized the throne, requesting that the Ministry of Works be commanded to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education and inscribe the graduates’ names upon it.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the distinction of jinshi with honors.

Mao Zan 茅瓚: registered in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in an artisan household; an added-quota student of the county school, specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bangxian; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi’an, his grandfather Mao, and his father Lin, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Ru. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhen and Ke, and his wife was née Fang. He placed twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Cheng 羅珵: registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a military household; a student of the Directorate of Education, specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bangzhen; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-six years old, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Duo was a provincial graduate who served as Acting Assistant Instructor and was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Personnel. His grandfather Yongjun was an Instructor in the Directorate of Education and received successive honorary grants culminating in the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of Personnel. His father Qinde was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and his mother, née Kang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Dang, and his wife was née Yang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Wei 袁煒: registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household; an attached student of the county school, specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Maozhong; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wan, his grandfather Jian, and his father Ruzhou. His mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhao and Huan, his younger brother was Zhuo, and his wife was née Guan. He placed second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second Class: ninety-five men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Zhang Weiyi, courtesy name Shouzhong, was registered in a civilian household in Ansu County, Baoding Prefecture, in the metropolitan region (Zhili). A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Song; his grandfather, Heng; and his father, Yu, a county-school Instructor. His mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Weijing, and his younger brothers were Weishi, Weiji, Weiyun, and Weihan. He married a woman née Hu. He ranked first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Yingyun, courtesy name Conglong, was registered in a medical household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged forty-six, and born on the eighteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan; his grandfather, Yu, who held an honorary title for longevity; and his father, Jin. His mother was née Feng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Lei, and his younger brothers were Dian, Ji, and Pei. He married a woman née Sun. He ranked sixtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yuan, courtesy name Zongqian, was registered in a civilian household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Record of Rites, he was ninth in birth order, aged forty-six, and born on the twenty-third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhining, was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather, Cheng, was granted an honorary rank of the eighth grade. His father, Xuan, was a prefectural Vice Prefect, promoted in honorary rank to Chaolie dafu. His father's principal wife was née Chen; his birth mother was née Lin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ji, Yi, Pu, Han, Tai, Xun, and Shen. His younger brothers were Jun; Wei, accorded the cap and girdle of a Registry Manager; Che; Zhang, an Official for Righteousness, an honorary title; Yan, an Instructor in a subprefectural medical school; Can; Chu; Zhi; Fa; Han; Miao; and Yong. He married a woman née Lu. He ranked thirty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Mo Ruzhong, courtesy name Ziliang, was registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ang; his grandfather, Hao, was an assistant prefect; his father, Yu, was a tribute scholar; and his mother was née Zhu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ruxin, Rude, Rujue, and Ruyi. He married a woman née Fu and subsequently a woman née Yang. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Shidao, courtesy name Zizhuan, was registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Changzhou County. A prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather, Wei; his father, Ping; and his mother, née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Andao. He married a woman née Cao and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed thirty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lun Yishen, courtesy name Yanqun, was registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yu. His grandfather, Ming, received the honorary title of Senior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy. His father, Wenxu, was Right Mentor in the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Expositor-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy, and was posthumously awarded the titles of Grand Master for Court Discussion and Chancellor of the Nanjing Directorate of Education. His mother, née Ou, received the title of Grand Lady of Respect. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yiliang, a Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, and Yixun, Chancellor of the Nanjing Directorate of Education. His younger brothers were Yimo, Yimou, Yichen, Yiqian, Yi'e, Yidang, Yizi, Yicheng, Yimi, Yizan, and Yifang. He married a woman née Deng. He placed twentieth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Guozuo, courtesy name Junying, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-one years old, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Jingda; his grandfather, Xuewen; his father, Shikong; and his mother, née Zheng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Guolie, Guozhao, Guoxiu 國休, and Guoxiu 國烋. He married a woman née Huang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qiao Shining, registered in a military household in Yaozhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jingshu; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the eighteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Zhiyu, and his father Zhongjie; his father’s former wife was née Yao, his mother née Li, and his stepmother née Bai. His father was living. His younger brother Shiding held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness. He married a woman née Song. He placed first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Zheng, registered in a military household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an added-quota student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhuangyu; he ranked third in birth order, was aged eighteen, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chao, his grandfather Wenxiang, who held an honorary official title for longevity, and his father Liangyu; his mother was née Huo. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Zhao and Jun, and his younger brother was Jie. He was betrothed to a woman née Chen. He placed first in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Chun, registered in a civilian household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yirong; he ranked nineteenth in birth order, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Jiamo held an honorary official title for longevity. His grandfather Shouxu was posthumously awarded the titles of Grand Master for Governance and Bureau Director in the Ministry of War. His father Daonan was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of War, and his mother, née Shu, was invested with the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tai, Feng, and Zou, the latter two being students of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Zhen and Quan [?], the latter also a student of the Directorate of Education. He married a woman née Xia. He placed tenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Kun, registered in an artisan household in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Meizhi; he ranked fourth in birth order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the eleventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather Bo’ang was posthumously awarded the titles of Grand Master of the Palace and Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud. His grandfather Zhang was awarded the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice and posthumously awarded the titles of Grand Master of the Palace and Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud. His father Hong was Minister of Justice at Nanjing, advanced in rank to Grand Master for Fostering Virtue and Senior Minister of Orthodox Governance, and posthumously awarded the title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent. His father’s former wives were née Wang, posthumously awarded the title of Lady, and née Xia, posthumously awarded the title of Lady of Gentleness; his mother, née Wang, was invested with the title of Lady. His mother was living. His elder brothers were Shan, Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate and formerly Right Vice Censor-in-Chief; Yan, Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; and Jiao, formerly Archivist in the Court of Imperial Entertainments. He married a woman née Chen, then successively women née Wang and Hong. He placed eighty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yao Zhang, registered in a civilian household in Yuanling County, Chenzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruyu; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zongxian, a county magistrate; his grandfather was Rang; and his father was Shitai, an honorary official for charitable service. His father’s former wife was née He, his legal mother née Li, and his birth mother née Tong. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Qiong, Ying, and Rui, and his younger brothers Wei and Xuan. He married a woman née Xiao. He placed first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 277th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Kui, registered in a civilian household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Wenming; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Ben, and his father Xuan. His mother was née Chen, and his successive stepmothers were née Wu 吳 and Wu 伍. His father was living and his mother deceased. He married a woman née Zhu and subsequently a woman née Wu 吳. He placed forty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Lian, registered in a civilian household in Anzhou, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Boqing; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather was Mian, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); and his father was Hanqing, an assistant instructor. His mother was née Zhuang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Lan was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Zhang. He placed 124th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Ziyi, registered in a civilian household in Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuji; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was He, his grandfather Jing, and his father Long. His mother was née Qiao. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Zixiao and Zipei. He married a woman née Huang. He placed eighty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Jian, registered in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military salt-producing household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weichun; he ranked tenth in his family and was thirty-seven years old, born on the third day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Wenyu, was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Rites. His grandfather, Zuo, was granted the titles Hanlin Academy Compiler and Gentleman for Rendering Service, and posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Rites. His father, Zan, was Right Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing and was posthumously granted the title Minister of Rites. His mother, née Ying, was granted the title Lady (shuren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tui, Yu (a student of the Directorate of Education), Qiao, Bei, Fu (a student of the Directorate of Education), Hui, Ao, Ting (Office Manager in the Nanjing Censorate [?]), and Cui; his younger brother was Zuo. He married a woman née Dai. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Yizhong, registered in Xinjian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chongyi; he ranked fifth in his family and was forty years old, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yongzhi, his grandfather Yi, his father Dazhang, and his mother née Cheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yicheng. He married a woman née Yu. He placed sixty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wen, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he ranked second in his family and was forty-two years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather, Zong, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity. His father, Ze, was granted the title Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and his mother, née Qian, was granted the title Lady of Repose (anren). Both parents were living. His elder brother, Zhao, was a Subprefectural Vice Magistrate and formerly a Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his younger brother was Zi. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Yuan. He placed twenty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Qian, registered in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yifu; he ranked fourth in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather, Qin, was a County Registrar; his grandfather was Yuan, and his father Sheng. His father's former wife was née Hao, and his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Jie. He married a woman née Liu. He placed ninety-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and three hundred and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

燕楫〔貫直隸真定府真定縣，民籍，府學生，治禮記，字廷濟，行三，年二十七，正月十八日生〕。曾祖恕〔所吏目〕，祖雲〔贈監察御史〕，父澄〔府同知，前監察御史〕，母李氏〔封孺人〕。永感下，兄𣐍〔監生〕、桂〔七品散官〕，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第二十四名，會試第三百十四名。
translation_en:
Zhu Yong, of Henan Guard in Henan, was registered in a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Boji. He was first in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Tong, and his father Yong; his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhou, and his wife was née Shen. He placed eleventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Mu, of Qiongshan County, Qiongzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Jingwen. He was first in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the second day of the first month. His great-grandfather Qiansheng and grandfather Zheng were each posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Revenue. His father Zhou was Left Vice Minister of Revenue, and his mother, née Zhong, was granted the title of Lady of Virtue. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhi and Jia. His wife was née Li; he subsequently married a woman née Gao. He placed fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Tingchen, of Hongtong County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was registered in a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Bolin. He was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fourteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xian. His grandfather Gong was an honorary official and was granted the title of Deputy Commander of a Police Office. His father Rong was a Prefectural Assistant Magistrate. His father's principal wife, née Ji, was granted the title of Lady; his birth mother was née Lin. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother Tingxiang was a tribute scholar; his younger brothers were Tingbi and Tingpin. His wife was née Duan. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Ji, of Zhending County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in a civilian household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Tingji. He was third in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the eighteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather Shu was a Clerk of a subprefectural office [?]. His grandfather Yun was posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor. His father Cheng was a Prefectural Vice Prefect and formerly an Investigating Censor; his mother, née Li, was granted the title of Lady. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were 𣐍 [name reading uncertain], an Imperial University student, and Gui, an official holding a seventh-rank prestige title. His wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 314th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Xian 陳憲 was registered in a civilian household in Jiaxing County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Daofu; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Zhao, his father Qing, and his mother Lady Li. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Cai, Hong, and Zhou. He married Lady Liu and subsequently Lady Jin. He placed tenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Changji 陳昌積 was registered in a military household in Taihe County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zifa; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhengda, his grandfather Bixun, his father Zhude, and his mother Lady Luo. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Deming, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; Dewen, a tribute student; Changmo; and Changjun. His younger brother Changfu was a District Magistrate. He married Lady Luo and subsequently Lady Zhu. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Huai 謝淮 was registered in a civilian household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Gaoyang County. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuhui; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ju, his grandfather Zhen, his father Fang, and his mother Lady Wang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Zhen, and his younger brothers were Jiang and Wei. He married Lady Bian and subsequently another Lady Bian. He placed sixteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Ruliang 侯汝諒 was registered in an official household of the Taiyuan Left Guard, Shanxi, and was an added-quota student at a prefectural school associated in the text with Hua County in the directly administered metropolitan region [?]. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shuzhen; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-four, born on the ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather Shouxian and grandfather Sheng both held the prestige title General of Military Strategy and served as Vice Battalion Commanders. His father Lun was Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Studs. His father's former wife, Lady Yu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace; his mother, Lady Wang, was granted the same title. His mother was deceased, and he attended his surviving father. His elder brothers were Ruzhong, a Vice Battalion Commander; Ruqian; Rune; Ruduan; and Ruhui. His younger brothers were Rushen, Ruchen, and Rujing. He married Lady Yan. He placed nineteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Weng Dali, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Rucan, and he ranked first in his family. He was twenty-two, born on the twenty-eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min, his grandfather Quan, and his father Zuo; his mother was née Yang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Ci, and his younger brothers were Dayin, Dazhang, and Dayi. His wife was née Jiang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qiu, registered in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Kejing, and he ranked 119th in his family. He was thirty-four, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingshen, his grandfather Tingjun, and his father Xuan. His father's former wife was née Xu, his mother née Zhu, and his stepmother née Qiu. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhuo, a prefectural vice prefect; Feng, a county magistrate; Jin; Hua, a school instructor; Si, a former investigating censor; Qian; and He. His younger brother was Chu. His wife was née Ye. He placed ninety-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Maozhi, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Junben, and he ranked first in his family. He was twenty, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji, a commissioner of a commercial tax office; his grandfather Duo held the title of honorary official. His father was Huan, his mother née Fang, and his stepmother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yingbiao, a surveillance vice commissioner; Yuntong, a surveillance assistant commissioner; Yingcai, a tribute scholar; Yinggui; Yingshu; and Yinglu. His younger brothers were Yinggou, Yingtan, and Yingsu. He was betrothed to a woman née Wu. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Min, registered in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Qinfu, and he ranked fifth in his family. He was thirty-seven, born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kongzhao, his grandfather Mengzhi, and his father Chenshi; his mother was née Liao and his stepmother née Deng. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jing, and his younger brothers were Jiao and Xiao. His wife was née Gong. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jin, registered in a military household in Dangtu County, Taiping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Chongnan; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lisan; his grandfather, Tong, was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Upright Service and Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue. His father, Jian, was a Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his mother, née Zhang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Luan, and his wife was née Xu. He placed fortieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Bi was registered in an officer household of the Nanjing Yulin Right Guard and was a native of Xuyi County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he had the courtesy name Guoxian, ranked second among his brothers, and was thirty-nine years old, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Wen, grandfather, Zhen, and father, Sheng, were all Commanders. His mother was née Guo. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother, Xi, was a Battalion Commander; his younger brothers were Ying and Run. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He placed eighty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Qi was registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Wujiang County. A National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he had the courtesy name Ziyou, ranked fourth among his brothers, and was forty-one years old, born on the twenty-first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan; his grandfather, Ben, held a seventh-rank prestige title; his father, Jing, was an Instructor of Medicine. His father's former wife was née Fang, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ao and Yue, both Subprefectural Clerks, and Shan; his younger brothers were Yan and Dai, the latter a National University student. His wife was née Guo. He placed fortieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 300th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hong Shiwen, registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Guohua; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Ying, held the title Grand Master for Fostering Virtue and served as Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather, Chang, was a student admitted by imperial grace; his father, Xuan, was a District Magistrate. His legal mother was née Zheng, and his birth mother was née Huang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Shiqian, and his wife was née Deng. He placed fiftieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Yiyuan 侯一元 was registered in a civilian household in Yueqing County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county government student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Shunju and ranked third in his family. He was twenty-eight years old, born on the sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ren; his grandfather, Jing, was a subprefectural judge and received the honorary appointment of Secretary in the Ministry of Rites. His father, Tingxun, was a Vice Prefect and formerly a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel. His mother, née Chen, was granted the title Lady of Peace (anren); his stepmother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yikui, an Imperial University student, Shouyu, Yiyang, and Yizhong; his younger brothers were Yigong, Shouheng, Yilin, Shoushou, and Yifeng. His wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bi Jingrong 畢竟容 was registered in a military household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Record of Rites, he had the courtesy name Renshu and ranked fifty-seventh in his family. He was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather, Keng; and his father, Yinqing. His mother was née Hua, and his stepmother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jingke. His wife was née Li; he subsequently married a woman née Lü. He placed seventeenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bai Ruogui 白若圭 was registered in an official household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Record of Rites, he had the courtesy name Dechun and ranked second in his family. He was twenty-seven years old, born on the fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather, Ang, was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Justice; he was posthumously granted the titles Specially Advanced and Grand Guardian, with the posthumous name Kangmin. His grandfather, Qi, was Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission in the Office of Transmission and was posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father, Zhao, was an Office Manager in the Court of State Ceremonial. His father's principal wife was née Zhang; his stepmothers were née Chen, Zheng, and Sheng; his birth mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chou. His younger brothers were Ou; Ruosi, an Imperial University student; Zhuo, an Imperial University student; Qideng; Ru, an Imperial University student; Kan; Ruoshui, an Imperial University student; Cheng; Qichang; Qitai; Ruobi; and Ruoquan. His wife was née Wang. He placed twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Yuanbi 吳元璧 was registered in a military household in Anren County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Junxi and ranked tenth in his family. He was forty years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Kesi; his grandfather, Xing, held the honorary title of Philanthropic Official; and his father was Shangda. His mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuancheng and Yuanhan; his younger brother was Yuangong. His wife was née Ai; he subsequently married a woman née Li. He placed twenty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

聞人悳行〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，府學生，治禮記，字元科，行一，年二十七，九月初八日生〕。曾祖籌，祖言〔縣主簿〕，父莊，母徐氏，繼母鄭氏。重慶下，弟悳容、悳業、悳教、悳隆、悳化、悳政、悳敷、悳應，娶于氏。浙江鄉試第十名，會試第三十七名。

俞憲〔貫直隸常州府無錫縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字汝成，行一，年三十一，三月初八日生〕。曾祖公元，祖廷俊，父暉，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄岳，弟寰、寅、官、寀、賓、寔、宣，娶張氏。應天府鄉試第六十三名，會試第一百九十五名。

張鎬〔貫直隸保定府定興縣民籍，陝西涇陽縣人，國子生，治春秋，字啓周，行三，年三十八，六月二十日生〕。曾祖見，祖材，父景芳〔壽官〕，母李氏。具慶下，兄錦、銓〔冠帶將軍〕，弟𨱑，娶趙氏，繼娶徐氏。順天府鄉試第五名，會試第一百四十七名。

周鯤〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字少魚，行二，年三十二，四月十八日生〕。曾祖輦〔訓導〕，祖俅〔訓導，贈監察御史〕，父宣〔布政使司左布政使〕，母陳氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，兄鰲，娶柯氏。福建鄉試第七十三名，會試第二百十一名。
translation_en:
Wenren Dexing, registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Yuanke; he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chou; his grandfather, Yan, was a County Registrar; his father was Zhuang; his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother née Zheng. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Derong, Deye, Dejiao, Delong, Dehua, Dezheng, Defu, and Deying. He married a woman née Yu. He placed tenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Xian, registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Rucheng; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty-one, born on the eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongyuan; his grandfather, Tingjun; his father, Hui; and his mother, née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yue; his younger brothers were Huan, Yin, Guan, Cai, Bin, Shi, and Xuan. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Gao, registered in a civilian household in Dingxing County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a native of Jingyang County, Shaanxi, and a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Qizhou; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twentieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Cai; his father, Jingfang, held an honorary title for longevity; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jin and Quan, the latter a general granted the cap and sash of rank [?]; his younger brother was Huang. He married a woman née Zhao and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Kun, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shaoyu; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Nian, was an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather, Qiu, was an Assistant Instructor posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father, Xuan, was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; and his mother, née Chen, was granted the title of Lady. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Ao. He married a woman née Ke. He placed seventy-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

王輪〔貫山西平陽府蒲州，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字子庸，行一，年三十二，二月初五日生〕。曾祖𤉧，祖寅，父珪，母張氏，繼母祁氏、李氏、高氏。慈侍下，弟軫，聘楊氏，娶何氏。山西鄉試第十八名，會試第三十三名。

黃懋官〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，民籍，府學附學生，治詩經，字君辨，行六，年二十三，十月初二日生〕。曾祖仲昭〔按察司提學僉事，進階朝列大夫，前翰林院編修〕，祖乾剛〔贈承德郎，南京戶部署員外郎〕，父希濩〔知縣〕，母鄭氏。重慶下，兄懋宣、懋道、允〔光祿寺署丞〕、尚〔生員〕、磨謙〔貢士〕，弟懋寬、懋敬、懋中、懋良、懋直、懋晃，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第五十三名，會試第二百八十五名。

葉選〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字仁夫，行三，年三十六，六月十五日生〕。曾祖詵，祖世榮，父景賢，母史氏，繼母嚴氏。具慶下，兄迪，弟遜、建、述、迅、逵、週，聘徐氏，娶羅氏。浙江鄉試第二十名，會試第二百四十一名。

張朝聘〔貫陝西西安府長安縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯時，行一，年二十九，六月初七日生〕。曾祖鼎，祖英，父璉，母王氏。永感下，娶王氏，繼娶施氏。陝西鄉試第三十七名，會試第二百五十六名。
translation_en:
Wang Lun 王輪 was registered in a military household in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Ziyong and was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, born on the fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was 𤉧 [reading uncertain]; his grandfather, Yin; his father, Gui; his mother, née Zhang; and his stepmothers, née Qi, Li, and Gao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Zhen. He was betrothed to a woman née Yang and married a woman née He. He ranked eighteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Maoguan 黃懋官 was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Junbian and was sixth in birth order, aged twenty-three, born on the second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Zhongzhao, was an Education Intendant serving as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, advanced to the rank of Grand Master for Court Service, and formerly a Compiler in the Hanlin Academy. His grandfather, Qiangang, was posthumously granted the rank of Gentleman for Fostering Virtue and served as acting Vice Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue. His father, Xihuo, was a District Magistrate; his mother was née Zheng. His parents and members of the grandparental generation were living. His elder brothers were Maoxuan, Maodao, Yun (an Office Assistant in the Court of Imperial Entertainments), Shang (a government student), and Moqian [?] (a tribute student). His younger brothers were Maokuan, Maojing, Maozhong, Maoliang, Maozhi, and Maohuang. He married a woman née Chen. He ranked fifty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Xuan 葉選 was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Renfu and was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, born on the fifteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Shen; his grandfather, Shirong; his father, Jingxian; his mother, née Shi; and his stepmother, née Yan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Di; his younger brothers were Xun, Jian, Shu, Xun, Kui, and Zhou. He was betrothed to a woman née Xu and married a woman née Luo. He ranked twentieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chaopin 張朝聘 was registered in a civilian household in Chang’an County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Boshi and was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, born on the seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Ding; his grandfather, Ying; his father, Lian; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Shi. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Xianqing, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household. He was a supplementary student at the county school and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Lianfu; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mao, his grandfather Cong, his father Yu, and his mother née Du. His mother alone was still living. He married a woman née Gu. He ranked tenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tingchun, registered in Yugan County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household. He was an added-quota student at the county school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Maoren; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhan, his grandfather Jing, his father Xian, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tingxiang, Tingdui, Tingshi, Tingyu, and Tingshi. He was betrothed to a woman née Liu. He ranked twenty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Zhong, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household. He was a supplementary student at the county school and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhifu; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao, his grandfather Chen, his father Ang, and his mother née Zou. Both parents were living. His younger brother was He. He married a woman née Chen. He ranked sixty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Bi, registered in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household. He was a student at the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenfu; he was twelfth in birth order, aged forty-eight, and born on the thirteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yin; his grandfather Zhen held the honorary title of Righteous Official; his father Yuan was a Consort; and his mother was the Lady of Yongchuan Commandery. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lu, Zan, Qi, Xuan, and Huan. His younger brothers were Mao, Bao (a Consort), Yu, Hu (a Consort), Lian (a Consort), and Jie (a Consort). He married a woman née Wang. He ranked tenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳鎏，貫直隸蘇州府吳縣，匠籍，縣學附學生。治《易經》，字子兼，行二，年三十三，三月二十三日生。曾祖寧〔王府教授〕，祖懷，父冕，前母沈氏，母莫氏。具慶下，娶曹氏，繼娶韓氏。應天府鄉試第二名，會試第四十二名。

譚維，貫四川潼川州蓬溪縣，民籍，國子生。治《易經》，字元立，行九，年四十七，五月二十五日生。曾祖必成，祖宣〔知縣〕，父宗簡〔封監察御史〕，母陳氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，兄珪、儼、价、冠〔府同知〕、采〔鹽倉大使〕、纘〔按察司副使〕、純〔義官〕，弟繼〔監生〕，娶張氏。四川鄉試第三十七名，會試第一百七十一名。

王楠，貫直隸興州後屯衛，官籍，浙江會稽縣人，三河縣學生。治《詩經》，字惟喬，行四，年四十六，九月二十日生。曾祖忠〔指揮僉事，贈錦衣衛都指揮同知〕，祖鑑〔指揮僉事，贈錦衣衛都指揮同知〕，父玉〔錦衣衛都指揮同知，充漕運參將〕，母邢氏〔封夫人〕。永感下，兄桐，弟楊〔兵部員外郎〕、棟、相、栩、槐，娶袁氏。順天府鄉試第四十三名，會試第一百六名。

劉志，貫山西平陽府翼城縣，民籍，國子生。治《易經》，字寧卿，行三，年三十六，正月初九日生。曾祖復嚴，祖翥〔恩例冠帶〕，父玶〔訓導〕，母曹氏。具慶下，兄愈，弟悊、聰，娶李氏。山西鄉試第七名，會試第三百十三名。
translation_en:
Chen Liu, registered in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zijian. He ranked second in birth order and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ning (Professor in a princely establishment), his grandfather Huai, and his father Mian; his father's former wife was née Shen, and his mother was née Mo. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Cao and subsequently a woman née Han. He placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tan Wei, registered in Pengxi County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yuanli. He ranked ninth in birth order and was forty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bicheng, his grandfather Xuan (District Magistrate), and his father Zongjian (honorarily invested as Investigating Censor); his mother was née Chen (honorarily invested as Lady of Respect). His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Gui, Yan, Jie, Guan (Vice Prefect), Cai (Salt Granary Commissioner), Zuan (Surveillance Vice Commissioner), and Chun (Honorary Official); his younger brother was Ji (student of the Directorate of Education). He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Nan, registered in the Xingzhou Rear Garrison Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an official household. He was originally from Kuaiji County, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Sanhe County school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weiqiao. He ranked fourth in birth order and was forty-six years old, born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhong and grandfather Jian were both Assistant Commanders, each posthumously granted the title of Vice Commissioner-in-Chief of the Embroidered-uniform Guard. His father Yu was Vice Commissioner-in-Chief of the Embroidered-uniform Guard, serving as Assistant Regional Commander for grain transport; his mother was née Xing (honorarily invested as Lady). Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Tong; his younger brothers were Yang (Vice Director in the Ministry of War), Dong, Xiang, Xu, and Huai. He married a woman née Yuan. He placed forty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhi, registered in Yicheng County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ningqing. He ranked third in birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuyan, his grandfather Zhu (granted the cap and girdle of official status under provisions for imperial favor), and his father Ping (Assistant Instructor); his mother was née Cao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yu; his younger brothers were Zhe and Cong. He married a woman née Li. He placed seventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 313th in the Metropolitan Examination.

章煥〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣，民籍，吳縣人，國子生，治易經，字懋實，行二，年三十四，七月十一日生。〕曾祖思恭，祖澄，父棟，母唐氏，繼母魯氏。具慶下，兄炤，弟燦、爌、燁、焯，娶沈氏。應天府鄉試第一百二十二名，會試第三百十七名。

蔣懷德〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣，民籍，府學生，治詩經，字維靈，行十四，年三十九，九月二十日生。〕曾祖玉，祖孝，父實，母潘氏。嚴侍下，兄懷正、懷義、懷遠，弟懷禮、懷貞，娶呂氏，繼娶王氏、趙氏。浙江鄉試第六十八名，會試第七名。
translation_en:
Xu Wei 徐緯, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wencheng, and he ranked forty-third in his family. He was aged twenty-nine [?; the transcription has 平 in place of the expected 年], born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Gang, his father Zao, and his mother née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiu, Ji, and Qi; his younger brothers were Shou, Xian, Yan, Wan, and Luo. His wife was née Zhou. He placed twenty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Tinghu 鄭廷鵠, registered in Hainan Guard, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was a native of Yueqing County, Zhejiang. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanshi, and he ranked first in his family. He was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Shunzong, his father Wen, and his mother née Yu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Hai. He placed nineteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Huan 章煥, registered in Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Wu County. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Maoshi, and he ranked second in his family. He was aged thirty-four, born on the eleventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Sigong, his grandfather Cheng, his father Dong, his mother née Tang, and his stepmother née Lu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhao; his younger brothers were Can, Kuang, Ye, and Zhuo. His wife was née Shen. He placed 122nd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 317th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Huaide 蔣懷德, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weiling, and he ranked fourteenth in his family. He was aged thirty-nine, born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Xiao, his father Shi, and his mother née Pan. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Huaizheng, Huaiyi, and Huaiyuan; his younger brothers were Huaili and Huaizhen. His first wife was née Lü; his subsequent wives were née Wang and née Zhao. He placed sixty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qing Wenrui, courtesy name Ruxian, was registered in an artisan household in Gong'an County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in family order and was forty years old, born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lun; his grandfather was Xi, an honorary official for longevity; his father was Cheng; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Wenyuan. He married a woman née Zhu and subsequently a woman née Tian. He placed forty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Weiping, courtesy name Shude, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in family order and was twenty-five years old, born on the third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhao, Director of a county school, posthumously awarded the title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War; his grandfather was Yingxing; his father was Zhizong; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Weihan. He married a woman née Lin. He placed ninetieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 319th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Xixian, courtesy name Jifu, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in family order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tizi; his grandfather was Zhao; his father was Liangpu; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xisheng, and his younger brothers were Xiwu, Xiying, Xican, Xiyan, Xixian, Xiqu, and Xilian. He married a woman née Xu. He placed fifty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xu, courtesy name Bangli, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked sixteenth in family order and was forty-four years old, born on the twelfth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengyan; his grandfather was Heng, an Assistant Instructor; his father was Wenbin; and his mother was née Song. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yunqu, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), Yuncheng, Yunjie, and Mu. He married a woman née Yu. He placed sixty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhou Nan, registered in the guardsman register of the Ceremonial Guard Office of Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Wenhua; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Shiyuan, his grandfather Fuhao, his father Yu, and his mother née Pan. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dunren, registered in the civilian register of Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhong’an; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the tenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Wenbing, his grandfather Ning (Assistant Instructor), his father Qin (Instructor), and his mother née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Dunhou, and his younger brothers were Dunhua and Dunfu (tribute scholar, gongshi). He married a woman née Pan. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Huan, registered in the civilian register of Shanyang County, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yanghui; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Sheng, his father Gui, and his mother née Ye. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Can and Xun, and his younger brothers Bing and Gao. He married a woman née Liu. He placed sixty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Nan Fengji, registered in the military register of Weinan County, Hua Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanzhen; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-five, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yan, his grandfather Gui, his father Jin (Instructor, additionally awarded the posthumous titles of Grand Master for Governance and Director in the Ministry of Revenue), and his mother née Jiao (additionally granted the title of Senior Lady of Suitability). Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Daji (Prefect). He married a woman née Li. He placed third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lü Yong 呂顒, courtesy name Youcheng, was registered in a civilian household in Ningzhou, Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, an Assistant Subprefect; his grandfather was Sheng, posthumously granted the prestige title Zhengshilang and the office of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites; his father was Jing, formerly Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; and his mother, née Gao, was granted the title Lady (ruren). His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother, Zhuan, was a Prefect; his younger brothers were Ban, Shuo, and Yu. His wife was née Zhou. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xin Xuanran 辛烜然, courtesy name Yanghui, was registered in a military household in Shizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather was Wenyuan, a Prefect; and his father was Zhu, an Assistant Prefect. His mother, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren), and his stepmother, née Hao, was granted the same title. His father and stepmother were both living. His elder brother was Yuran, and his younger brothers were Xiran and Yueran. His wife was née Wen. He placed forty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Chu 徐楚, courtesy name Shiwang, was registered in a civilian household in Chun’an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng, his grandfather was Yuan, his father was Rang, and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Mao and Fen. His first wife was née Lu, and his subsequent wife was née Hong. He placed eighty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Kan 蔣坎, courtesy name Yangfu, was registered in a military household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked eleventh among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ning, his grandfather was Cong, his father was Shi, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kun, Lin, Dashan [?], Ding, Huan, Tai, and Shi. His wife was née Huang. He placed eighty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Tongyan, courtesy name Defu, was registered in a military household in Changqing County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-two years old, born on the nineteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather, Ming, was a Police Chief; his father, Yongzhi, was an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tongren, and his younger brothers were Tongxiang, Tongxian, Tongcai, and Tongli. His wife was née Li. He placed sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Ruzhou, courtesy name Jiqing, was registered in a salt-producing household in Chongde County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Mengxiong, his father Fu, and his mother née Qian. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Rujing and Rulin, and his younger brothers were Ruli, Ruyan, Ruxun, and Ruxing. His wife was née Chen. He placed eighty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Ruolin, courtesy name Zicai, was registered in a military household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Fengyi, was a county school Instructor, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Governance and Left Mentor of the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Reader in the Hanlin Academy. His grandfather, Duanming, was Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate; his father, Han, was an Imperial University student admitted through the annual tribute quota; and his mother was née Lu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Ruoshu, a tribute scholar, Ruozhi, Ruozhu, Ruoguo, and Ruomei. His wife was née Weng. He placed twenty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Weng Xiang, courtesy name Changqing, was registered in a military household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and belonged to the Hangzhou Right Guard. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the twenty-third day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xiang; his grandfather, Mao, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his father was Hao; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cheng and Chun, and his younger brothers were Jia and Nan. His wife was née Sun. He placed forty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tang Chen, registered in an officer household of Daxing Left Guard and a native of Tianchang County in the directly administered region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhijing, and he ranked first in birth order. He was thirty-one, born on the ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Jie; and his father, Xiang. His father's former wife was née Wei, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Ren. He placed ninety-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jixian, registered in a civilian household of Luzhou, Sichuan, was a student of the department school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Boxiao, and he ranked first in birth order. He was thirty-three, born on the twenty-third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather, Xun, was posthumously granted the title of Prefectural Judge; his grandfather, Fuchu, was a Department Magistrate. His father was Song, and his mother was née He. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Jideng, Jisheng, and Jichang; his younger brothers were Jixian (繼賢) and Jixue. His wife was née Wu. He placed sixteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Mu, registered in an artisan household of Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shunbin, and he ranked sixth in birth order. He was thirty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shangwen; his grandfather, Ti; and his father, Lin, who held an honorary rank for longevity. His mother was née Zhong. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Ji, Zhi, and He. His wife was née Xu. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shijian, registered in a civilian household of Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Benjie, and he ranked fourth in birth order. He was forty-two, born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongdao; his grandfather, Ji; and his father, Jin. His father's former wife was née Huang, and his mother was née Su. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shiyang, Shiwen, Shitong, Shiliang, and Shigong; his younger brothers were Shizhan, Shirang, Shida, and Shixian. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fifty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Shaoru, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shikong; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-three, and was born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sixian; his grandfather, Gong, was an Assistant Instructor posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his father, Ao, held an eighth-rank prestige title; and his mother was née Tang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shaoshi, Shaoli, Tao, Huo, Yong, Shangzhi, Shaowen (a tribute scholar), and Shaowu; his younger brothers were Shaoyi, He, Zhun, Shaoqian, and Shaoxian. His wife was née Guan. He placed fifty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Huan, registered in Dingzhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenfu; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Lun, was a Prefect; his grandfather, Xuan, held an honorary official title for public benefaction; his father was Yong; his mother was née Wang; and his stepmother was née Zhou. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhu, Si, Huang, and Xiang. His wife was née Tian, and his subsequent wife was née Luo. He placed eighty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Mengyang, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was an attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shaoming; he ranked first in birth order, was aged twenty-one, and was born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather was Manshou; his father was Shiru; and his mother was née Huo. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Wu’an and Wubin. He was betrothed to a woman née You. He placed sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Qin, registered in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Maowen; he ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi; his grandfather, Da, was posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Qi, was a Prefect; and his mother, née Wang, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xianyue, Xiancen, Zhu, Lan, Shen (an Imperial Academy student), and Hui; his younger brothers were Wei (a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites), Xuan (a metropolitan graduate, jinshi), Kui (an Imperial Academy student), and Fei. His wife was née Min. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Hong, registered in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bozhan; he ranked fourteenth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged forty-three, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pa [?]; his grandfather, Xian, was a subprefectural assistant judge; his father, Sijing, was a district magistrate. His mother was née Lü, and his stepmother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Jing, Lun (a district vice magistrate), Gang (a district magistrate), Ji, Shou, and Shao; his younger brothers were Jin, Ji, and Yan. His wife was née Lü. He placed forty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chong, registered in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Rucheng; he ranked fourth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged forty-one, and was born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather Mei, and his father Zhen; his mother was née Meng. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Cai, Chen, and Xiao; his younger brother was Bin. His wife was née Xiao. He placed first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Geng, registered in Mianchi County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Rucai; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was aged forty, and was born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yan, was a district magistrate; his grandfather, Ying, held a seventh-rank prestige title. His father was Gan, and his mother was née Bi. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Xie. He placed sixty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Jiugao, registered in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruming; he ranked eleventh among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the ninth day of the intercalary first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Yi, an assistant prefect; his mother was née Ding. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jiushao; his younger brothers were Jiuchuan, Jiubao, and Jiushan. His wife was née Zhou. He placed sixty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.
