translation_en:
Sun Quan, courtesy name Wenkui, was a prefectural school student registered in a civilian household in Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; he specialized in the Book of Documents, was fifth in birth order, and was aged twenty-six, born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanrui; his grandfather, Bin, had been honorifically appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Cui, and his mother was née Hu, both living. His elder brothers were Ke, E, and Duo, and his younger brothers were Yue, Zhao, Gao, Xi, Yi, Yu, Kai, and Suo; his wife was née Zhou. He ranked seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhi, courtesy name Zishou, was a student of the Directorate of Education registered in a civilian household in Gushi County, Guangzhou Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan; he specialized in the Book of Documents, was third in birth order, and was aged thirty-three, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deshan, his grandfather was Ying, his father was Zheng, and his mother was née Xu; his father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Fu and Lu, and his wife was née Tian. He ranked forty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tang, courtesy name Shusi, was an added-quota student of the county school registered in a civilian household in Changsha County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang; he specialized in the Book of Changes, was second in birth order, and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather was Yuancong, his father was Zhongsheng, his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Tao; his father was deceased and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Xiang, and his wife was née Peng. He ranked twelfth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiamo, courtesy name Zhongchen, was a county school student registered in a military household in Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong; he specialized in the Book of Documents, was fourth in birth order, and was aged twenty-seven, born on the fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Pu, his grandfather was Qi, his father was Zi, and his mother was née Zhang, both parents living. His elder brothers were Cunren, Cunyi, and Jiayan, and his wife was née Fu. He ranked third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shen Youru, registered in a civilian household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zizhen; he ranked third in his family and was twenty-six years old, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather was Gao, an honorary official for longevity; his father was Jing, and his mother was née Xu. His grandfather and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Youren, Youlun, and Youqiao; his younger brothers were Youjia, Youxin, Youyi, and Yousi. His wife was née Dong. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shichun, registered in a military household in Guang Prefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yiyuan; he ranked first in his family and was thirty years old, born on the eighteenth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Kui; his grandfather was Zhi; his father was Wenzhang, and his mother was née Ji. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shixiao; his younger brothers were Shixian, Shiyang, Shixin, and Shiheng. His wife was née Liu. He placed fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Jianbang, registered in a civilian household in Ba Prefecture, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weixin; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Liang, a clerk in a guard; his grandfather was Fengyi, an honorary official for longevity; his father was Mo, an annual tribute student, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jianzi, and his wife was née Wang. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lian, registered in a civilian household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziqing; he ranked seventh in his family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Peng, an honorary official for philanthropy; his grandfather was Shou, an honorary official for longevity; his father was Yingzhen, an official awaiting selection for appointment, and his mother was née Wu. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Hong, Jiang, Chao, Shen, Yuan, and Han (a tribute scholar); his younger brothers were Zhe, Chun, Xun (a tribute scholar), Hao (an official awaiting selection for appointment), Can, Qu, Hong, Ting, Ji, Mu, Ying, Che, and Pan. His wife was née Shen. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

山西鄉試第三十五名　會試第一百五十九名
punctuated:
第三甲二百二十二名，賜同進士出身。

劉洵〔貫江西饒州府鄱陽縣軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字睿甫，行六十，年三十，閏九月十三日生〕。曾祖烈〔布政使司右參政，贈大中大夫資治少尹〕，祖城〔都察院右副都御史，贈通議大夫〕，父錄〔工部主事〕，母趙氏〔贈安人〕。嚴侍下，弟泌、法、沾、治、泳、冲、沚、浚，娶戴氏。順天府鄉試第五名，會試第二名。

張元冲〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字叔謙，行三十三，年三十七，七月十三日生〕。曾祖蘊輝〔封兵科給事中〕，祖以弘〔布政使司左參議〕，父景琦〔知府〕，母唐氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下，兄元楚、元本、元溥〔兵馬司副指揮〕、元傑、元亮，弟元敘、元萬、兀重，娶胡氏。浙江鄉試第八十六名，會試第二百八十九名。

裴紳〔貫山西平陽府蒲州軍籍，國子生，治書經，字子書，行一，年二十六，六月初六日生〕。曾祖賛，祖英〔壽官〕，父鼎，母張氏。具慶下，弟綬、純，娶陳氏。山西鄉試第三十五名，會試第一百五十九名。
translation_en:
Third class: 222 men, granted the status of graduates equivalent to metropolitan graduates (jinshi).

Liu Xun, of a military household registered in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Ruifu; he ranked sixtieth in family order and was thirty years old, born on the thirteenth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather Lie was Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, posthumously granted the honorary titles Grand Master of the Palace (dazhong dafu) and Junior Governor for Aid in Governance (zizhi shaoyin). His grandfather Cheng was Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate, posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Thorough Counsel (tongyi dafu). His father Lu was a Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his mother, née Zhao, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Tranquility. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Mi, Fa, Zhan, Zhi, Yong, Chong, Zhi, and Jun. He married a woman née Dai. He placed fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yuanchong, of a civilian household registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shuqian; he ranked thirty-third in family order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Yunhui was honorarily appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs. His grandfather Yihong was Left Administration Assistant Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; his father Jingqi was a Prefect. His mother, née Tang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yuanchu, Yuanben, Yuanpu, a Vice Commander in a Wardens’ Office, Yuanjie, and Yuanliang; his younger brothers were Yuanxu, Yuanwan, and Wuzhong [?]. He married a woman née Hu. He placed eighty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pei Shen, of a military household registered in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zishu; he ranked first in family order and was twenty-six years old, born on the sixth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zan; his grandfather Ying held an honorary official title for longevity. His father was Ding, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shou and Chun. He married a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

齊譽〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣民籍，府學增廣生，治詩經，字文實，行二，年二十八，十月初九日生〕。曾祖若山，祖王臣，父世懋，母龔氏。具慶下，兄警，弟變、言，娶萬氏。江西鄉試第八十一名，會試第三十六名。

translation_en:
Jiang Kun, registered in a civilian household in Yugan County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zipeng, he ranked twenty-eighth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was thirty-four sui, born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingjie, his grandfather Li, his father Chaozong, and his mother née Yu; his mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jing and Lin, his younger brothers Huang and Kuai, and his wife was née Shu. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Guangzhe, registered in a military household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Ziyu, he ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was thirty-one sui, born on the twenty-second day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hua, his grandfather Lin, his father Jing, and his mother née Wang; his parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Guangqi, his younger brothers Guanghu, Guangzhi, Guangshao, Guangtai, Guangzu, and Guangzhou, and his wife was née Yu. He placed twelfth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Yu, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional-quota student at the prefectural government school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wenshi, he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, and he was twenty-eight sui, born on the ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ruoshan, his grandfather Wangchen, his father Shimao, and his mother née Gong; both parents were living. His elder brother was Jing, his younger brothers Bian and Yan, and his wife was née Wan. He placed eighty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jingxian, registered in a civilian household in Meizhou, Sichuan, was a subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Mianzhi, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, and he was twenty-six sui, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Puzhong, posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Yuyan, a Prefect; his father was Hongyong, a tribute scholar (gongshi); and his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Xiangxian; he married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Guo. He placed sixty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

厲汝進〔貫直隸永平府灤州民籍，州學增廣生，治易經，字子脩，行三，年三十，十一月初四日生〕。曾祖翺，祖友諒，父鑑，母楊氏，繼母王氏。具慶下，兄章、汝成，娶薛氏。順天府鄉試第九名，會試第三十八名。
translation_en:
Li Lun 李綸, courtesy name Deyan, was registered in an official household of Huai’an Guard under the Wanquan Regional Military Commission and was a native of Yingshang County in Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Hong and grandfather Xian were both Battalion Judges. His father was Qin; his father’s former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Han. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shen, Ji, and Wei, and he married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Er [?] 潘𦓒, courtesy name Xixing, was registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the twentieth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Siwen was posthumously awarded the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of War. His grandfather was Ji, his father was Qi, his mother was née Dai, and his stepmother was née Hu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yu, a tribute scholar, Heng, and Tang; his younger brother was Jin. He married a woman née Dai and subsequently a woman née Hu. He placed fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Huai 陳淮, courtesy name Dongzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. He served as School Instructor in Puzhou, Shandong, and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. He ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather Ye was a provincial graduate (juren) who served as acting School Instructor; his grandfather Xiang was a Station Master. His father was Lian, his mother was née Lin, and his stepmother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Guan, and he married a woman née Wu. He placed thirty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Rujin 厲汝進, courtesy name Zixiu, was registered in a civilian household in Luanzhou, Yongping Prefecture, Zhili. An additional student of the department school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ao, his grandfather was Youliang, his father was Jian, his mother was née Yang, and his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhang and Rucheng, and he married a woman née Xue. He placed ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

張松〔貫河南河南府洛陽縣，匠籍，府學生，治易經，字汝喬，行一，年二十五，八月初二日生〕。曾祖成，祖傑，父臣，母韋氏。重慶下，弟梅、椿、榆、楨，娶蔡氏。河南鄉試第五十六名，會試第二百九十七名。

李棟〔貫湖廣辰州府盧溪縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字隆仲，行一，年三十六，十一月初九日生〕。曾祖茂，祖時勉〔壽官〕，父廷鶴，母楊氏。重慶下，兄樂〔南京戶部主事〕，弟柱、梧、栢、檟、樞，娶張氏。湖廣鄉試第十名，會試第一百四十三名。
translation_en:
Liu Tinggao, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruqin. He ranked twentieth in family order, was twenty-seven years old, and was born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Tan; his grandfather, Lian, was posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Rites; and his father was Hong. His father's former wife was née Hu, and his mother was née Fan. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Tingjie, Tingxun, Tingzhao, Tingyan, and Tingyi (a jinshi of the same examination cohort); his younger brothers were Tingqian, Tingrang, and Tingshi. He married a woman née Gui. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Liang, registered in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Kangmeng. He ranked first in family order, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather, Hong, was Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; his grandfather was Xiao; his father, Zuan, was a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Luo. Both parents survived. His younger brothers were Zhi, Tai, and Wen. He married a woman née Cheng and subsequently a woman née Ma. He placed twenty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Song, registered in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, belonged to an artisan household and was a student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruqiao. He ranked first in family order, was twenty-five years old, and was born on the second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather was Jie, his father was Chen, and his mother was née Wei. His parents and at least one grandparent survived. His younger brothers were Mei, Chun, Yu, and Zhen. He married a woman née Cai. He placed fifty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Dong, registered in Luxi County, Chenzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Longzhong. He ranked first in family order, was thirty-six years old, and was born on the ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Mao; his grandfather, Shimian, held an honorary official title awarded for longevity; his father was Tinghe; and his mother was née Yang. His parents and at least one grandparent survived. His elder brother, Le, was a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue at Nanjing; his younger brothers were Zhu, Wu, Bai, Jia, and Shu. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed tenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

朱執中〔貫浙江杭州府海寧縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字汝一，行二，年三十二，七月二十九日生〕。曾祖愷，祖坤，父鸞，母顧氏。重慶下，兄允中，弟時中、秉中、致中、懋中、思中、用中，聘許氏，娶呂氏。浙江鄉試第七十一名，會試第一百八十二名。

王士翹〔貫江西吉安府永新縣，民籍，安福縣縣學增廣生，治春秋，字民瞻，行一，年三十八，四月十三日生〕。曾祖猷允，祖槐兆，父寛，母劉氏，繼母朱氏。嚴侍下，兄敏〔官生〕、士俊〔知府〕，弟士翱，娶劉氏，繼娶劉氏。江西鄉試第三十五名，會試第二百八十七名。

顏嘉會〔貫湖廣長沙府攸縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字子亨，行二，年二十五，正月二十一日生〕。曾祖夔〔知縣〕，祖選〔衛經歷〕，父守忠〔知縣〕，母鍾氏。重慶下，兄嘉賓〔監生〕，弟嘉善、嘉慶、嘉兆，娶沈氏。湖廣鄉試第五十一名，會試第一百五十二名。
translation_en:
Feng Xuan, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tiqian. Fourth in family order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the eighteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather, Zhi, was a provincial graduate (juren) who served as acting Assistant Instructor; his father, Pu, held an honorary official title for longevity. His mother was née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Chao and Bing, and his younger brothers were Moran and Xu. He married a woman née Li. He placed fifty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Zhizhong, registered in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruyi. Second in family order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Kai, his grandfather Kun, and his father Luan; his mother was née Gu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Yunzhong, and his younger brothers were Shizhong, Bingzhong, Zhizhong, Maozhong, Sizhong, and Yongzhong. He was betrothed to a woman née Xu and married a woman née Lü. He placed seventy-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shiqiao, registered in Yongxin County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student of the Anfu County Confucian School. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Minzhan. First in family order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the thirteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Youyun, his grandfather Huaizhao, and his father Kuan; his mother was née Liu and his stepmother née Zhu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Min, a student admitted by virtue of official family status, and Shijun, a Prefect; his younger brother was Shi’ao. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently married another woman née Liu. He placed thirty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Jiahui, registered in You County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziheng. Second in family order, he was aged twenty-five and was born on the twenty-first day of the first month. His great-grandfather, Kui, was a District Magistrate; his grandfather, Xuan, was a Registrar in a Guard; his father, Shouzhong, was a District Magistrate. His mother was née Zhong. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother, Jiabin, was a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Jiashan, Jiaqing, and Jiazhao. He married a woman née Shen. He placed fifty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

魏尚綸〔貫河南鈞州儀衛司官籍，山東滕縣人，國子生，治書經，字仲一，行二，年三十五，八月十四日生〕。曾祖通，祖興，父宗〔儀衛司典仗〕，母張氏。具慶下，兄尚經，弟尚純〔戶部員外郎〕、尚絅，娶周氏，繼娶康氏。河南鄉試第二名，會試第九十六名。

translation_en:
Shi Jin, registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingshu, and he ranked fourth among his brothers. He was thirty-six, born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian, his grandfather Kui, and his father Biao; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zan and Xun, and his younger brothers Liang and Jian. He married a woman née Song. He placed forty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bao Long, registered in a civilian household in Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shihua, and he ranked fifth among his brothers. He was forty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo, his grandfather Zhixian, and his father Cai; his father’s former wife and his mother were both née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ming, Fan (Director of Foodstuffs), Ping, and Gong. He married a woman née Qin. He placed thirtieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 302nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Shanglun was registered in an official household attached to the Ceremonial Guard Office of Junzhou, Henan, and was originally from Teng County, Shandong. A National University student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongyi, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-five, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Xing, and his father Zong (Ceremonial Guard in the Ceremonial Guard Office); his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shangjing, and his younger brothers were Shangchun (Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue) and Shangjiong. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Kang. He placed second in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yi, registered in an artisan household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ruheng, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-nine, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongchu, his grandfather Congli, and his father Tingqi; his mother was née Fang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Zuohuang [?; possibly two brothers, Zuo and Huang]. He married a woman née Luo and subsequently a woman née Hu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳宗夔〔貫湖廣武昌府通山縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字惟一，行一，年三十二，三月初二日生〕。曾祖原甫〔壽官〕，祖珫〔監生〕，父與賢〔訓導〕，母吳氏。重慶下，弟宗蕃，娶宋氏。湖廣鄉試第四十六名，會試第二百九十名。

步允遷〔貫順天府薊州軍籍，山東高苑縣人，州學生，治禮記，字子安，行一，年二十四，八月初五日生〕。曾祖瀛，祖雄，父天衢〔貢士〕，母李氏。具慶下，娶孟氏。順天府鄉試第九十八名，會試第二百六十二名。
translation_en:
Xue Shangyi, registered in a civilian household in Hejian County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhongxing; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingchun, his grandfather Sheng, his father Long, and his mother née Gong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shangren, and his younger brothers were Shangli and Shangzhi. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Wanchao, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Yanghui; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Mixuan was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Prefect of Shuntian, and additionally Right Vice Minister of Revenue concurrently serving as Right Assistant Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His grandfather Lianggui was a Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, posthumously granted the title Right Vice Minister of Revenue concurrently serving as Right Assistant Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His father Fu held those latter concurrent offices. His father's former wife, née Huang, was posthumously granted the title Lady (shuren). His mother, née Weng, was granted the title Lady (ruren) and subsequently posthumously granted the higher title Lady (shuren). His stepmother was née Xu. Both parents were recorded as living. His elder brother Wanren was a student admitted by privilege as an official's son; his younger brothers were Jizu, Wanzai, Wanfeng, Wanshu, Jifan, and Wanyan. He married a woman née Zheng. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zongkui, registered in a military household in Tongshan County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Weiyi; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather Yuanfu held an honorary official title awarded for longevity; his grandfather Chong was an Imperial University student; his father Yuxian was an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Wu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Zongfan. He married a woman née Song. He ranked forty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bu Yunqian was registered in a military household in Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, and was a native of Gaoyuan County, Shandong. He was a subprefectural government school student specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Zi'an; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Xiong, his father Tianqu, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Meng. He ranked ninety-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

卜大同〔貫浙江嘉興府秀水縣，匠籍，國子生，治書經，字吉夫，行一，年三十，六月二十日生〕。曾祖顒，祖周〔義官〕，父宗洛〔監生〕，前母周氏，母賀氏。具慶下，弟大有、大觀、大順，娶周氏。順天府鄉試第七十名，會試第一百二名。

賈大亨〔貫浙江紹興府上虞縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字貞甫，行三，年四十，九月十二日生〕。曾祖章〔國子監典簿〕，祖暹〔教諭〕，父幼安，母陳氏。具慶下，兄大川，弟大節，娶羅氏。浙江鄉試第五十八名，會試第二百十六名。
translation_en:
Yang Yicheng, registered in Yichun County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Mingfu; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Donghui, his grandfather Bingji, his father Chunmei, and his mother née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yiqing, Yizheng, Ju [?], Yiqian, Yirang, Yijian, Yiliang, Yizhi, Yiqi, and Yiping. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ao Zongqing, registered in the Shuidejiang Native Chief’s Office, Sinan Prefecture, Guizhou, belonged to a civilian household and was originally from Xinyu County, Jiangxi. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rucheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuqin, his grandfather Lizhen, and his father Yuanyou; his father’s former wife was née Jian, and his mother was née Dong. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Guoqing and Jiaqing. He married a woman née Tian and subsequently a woman née Luo. He placed fiftieth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bu Datong, registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jifu; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twentieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather Zhou held the honorary title of Philanthropic Official; and his father Zongluo was a student of the Directorate of Education. His father’s former wife was née Zhou, and his mother was née He. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dayou, Daguan, and Dashun. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed seventieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Daheng, registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhenfu; he ranked third among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the twelfth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhang was an Archivist in the Directorate of Education; his grandfather Xian was a School Instructor; his father was You’an, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Dachuan, and his younger brother was Dajie. He married a woman née Luo. He placed fifty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Rudong, registered in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Bolong. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the thirteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Ying, and his father Sui; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ruliang, Runan (a tribute scholar, gongshi), and Rucai. His wife was née Chen. He ranked sixty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yi, registered in Taiping County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shunzhi. Sixteenth in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Defu, his grandfather Quan, and his father Benxiu; his mother was née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brothers were Bian and Ke. His wife was née Huang; he subsequently married a woman née Cheng. He ranked ninety-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Zhengxue, registered in Qianwei County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zichong. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Tianlu, and his father Shi (a prefect); his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhengxiu, Zhengji (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Zhengyan; his younger brother was Zhengxin. His wife was née Liu. He ranked sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Jie held official-household registration in the Daxing Left Guard and was a native of Yongqing County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was an added-quota student of the Shuntian Prefectural School and specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Erzhan. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the second day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin (a guard commander, posthumously granted the title General of Manifest Courage, Zhaoyong Jiangjun); his grandfather was Shen (a guard commander, granted the title General of Manifest Courage); and his father was Zhen (a guard commander). His mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ji and Di. His wife was née Guo. He ranked sixty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Zhu 黃注 was registered in a military household in Xinfeng County, Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Rulin; he ranked seventh among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ding; his grandfather, Xue, held honorary official status for charitable service; his father, Shui, was an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Gan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xun and Qi, and his younger brothers were Bian, Liu, and Zhu. His wife was née Lin. He placed twenty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jiuze 楊九澤 was registered in a civilian household in Huayin County, Huazhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zide; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was aged forty-one, and was born on the ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather, Hui, was a provincial graduate (juren) who served as acting School Instructor; his grandfather, Shen, held honorary official status for longevity; his father was Jinzhong; his mother was née Liu; and his successive stepmothers were née Wang and née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jiuyuan, Jiugong, Jiuchou, Jiujing, Jiuwei, Jiuguang, Jiuguan, and Jiushao. His wife was née Liu, and his subsequent wives were née Wang and née Liang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tingyi 劉廷儀 was registered with the Imperial Medical Institute and was a native of Cixi County, Zhejiang. He was a Shuntian prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruxiu; he ranked twentieth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the twenty-third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather was Jing, his father was Fan, and his mother was née Shao. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Tinggao, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort, Tingzhi, Tingyong, and Tingyin. His wife was née Feng. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Huang 張煌 was registered in a civilian household in Huai’an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a native of Min County. He was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yongtao; he ranked third among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hong, his grandfather was Yuan, his father was Bing, and his mother was née Dong. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brother was Xuan, and his wife was née Lin. He placed sixty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Bian, of civilian household registration in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, directly administered territory (Zhili), was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Bojing; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian, an honorary official for public beneficence; his grandfather was Bi, holder of a seventh-rank prestige title; his father was Yuanxi, a prefectural clerk; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ru and Han, both students of the Directorate of Education; Lian, a subprefectural clerk; Tong, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and Chun 淳. His younger brothers were Chun 湻, Han 瀚 (a student of the Directorate of Education admitted through the annual tribute quota), Yuan, Huai, and Shen. He married a woman née Cao. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xicheng, of military household registration in Lanyang County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zongyi; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, a subprefectural magistrate; his grandfather was Jin, an assistant instructor; his father was Jun, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Mao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xihan and Xi’ou. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Han. He placed thirteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Shulian, of military household registration in Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mingfa; he ranked eighth in birth order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dongche, his grandfather was Kuanjue, his father was Shendao, and his mother was née Ao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shuling and Shufang, and his younger brother was Shu’ai. He married a woman née Xiao and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed thirty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhichen, of civilian household registration in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanxiao; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twentieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng; his grandfather was Chong, an assistant instructor granted the honorary title of Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his father was Dong, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner, advanced to the prestige title of Grand Master for Court Service (Chaolie dafu); and his mother was née Zhao, granted the title of Lady of Respect. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Xuewen, Qin, Zhimin, Xueru, Zhiqing, and Zhishu; his younger brothers were Zhibin and Zhiyou. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 315th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Hongshi, of civilian registration in Zi County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yizhan; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the third day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Dakui, and his father Qin; his father's principal wife was née Ling, and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Honggui and Hongxuan, and his younger brother was Hongzhe. He married a woman née Tang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tan Qi, of civilian registration in Fu Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chaoqi; he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Benfang, his grandfather Zongxue, an honorary official appointed for public beneficence, and his father Ziwei; his mother was née Shen. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Hai, a County Vice Magistrate, and Dong, a ceremonial official (shengjiguan) [?]; his younger brothers were Rong, Tang, Jiang, and Nie. He married a woman née Huang. He placed fifty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yingji, of civilian registration in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the prefectural government school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Huinan; he ranked eleventh among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twelfth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Ruliang, a seventh-rank prestige official; his grandfather was Yong, an honorary official recognized for longevity and posthumously appointed a Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review. His father was Yan (䳡; reading uncertain [?]), an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His mother was née Zhu, posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren), and his stepmother was née Gu, granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yingbi, and his younger brothers were Yingchen and Yingdou. He married a woman née Wu. He placed thirty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zang Shan, of civilian registration in Shanyang County, Huai'an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student affiliated with the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zipei; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather Yue, and his father Hai, an honorary official recognized for longevity. His mother was née Gao, and his stepmother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hu, Lin (a National University student), Lian, Yuan, Zhu (a National University student), Ji, and Xuan. He married a woman née Tu. He placed 120th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Han Yiyou, registered in a civilian household in Qingcheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Rubi; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Xiang, and father, Qi, were county magistrates. His father's principal wife was née Jiao, and his birth mother was née Ma. His mother alone was surviving. His elder brother was Yizuo, and his younger brothers were Yidong and Yijing. He married a woman née Li. He placed fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yangzhi, registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhining, was posthumously appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather, Jue, was a prefect; and his father, Shi, was an assistant prefect. His mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother was née Huang. His father alone was surviving. His elder brothers were Yangmeng and Yangshi, the latter a government-supported school student; his younger brothers were Yangmin and Yangxing. He married a woman née Fu and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Shiyu, registered in a military household in Jingzhou, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Weimin; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Decai; his grandfather, Ning, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; and his father, Jide, was a county magistrate. His father's principal wife was née Sun, and his birth mother was née Pang. His mother alone was surviving. His elder brother was Shitong, and his younger brother was Shixuan. He married a woman née Wang. He placed ninety-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tingsong, registered in a civilian household in Ansu County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Maozhen; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was De; his grandfather was Ming; his father, Zheng, was a county vice magistrate; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were surviving. His elder brothers were Tinggui, an assistant prefect, and Tinghuai; his younger brothers were Tingwu and Tingmei. He married a woman née Wang. He placed 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhuge Xian, of a military household registered in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shujing, he ranked 136th in his family generation, and he was aged thirty-two [?; the transcription has 早 where 年, “age,” is expected], born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yantan; his grandfather, Zongxian, held the honorary designation “official for righteousness”; his father was Lang and his mother née Fan, both living; his elder brother was Shan, his younger brother Dai, and his wife née Wang; he placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Lin, of a military household registered in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was an added-quota county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zizhen, he ranked fourth in his family generation, and he was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yongcong, his grandfather Zheng, his father Yingxiang, and his mother née He; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Long and Jian, and he married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Xie; he placed eleventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Chong, of a civilian household registered in Dexing County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Junqing, he ranked nineteenth in his family generation, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the seventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Dan, was posthumously granted the title of County Magistrate; his grandfather, Jun, was a Department Magistrate; his father, Dun, held the honorary designation “official for righteousness”; his mother, née Wang, was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were An and Shou, his younger brothers Shi, Cheng, Cha, Ji, Yu, Mo, Zai, Mi, Ji, Qian, Xian, and Yan, and his wife was née Zhang; he placed seventy-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Weiyue, of an official household registered in Qingjian County, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zifu, he ranked second in his family generation, and he was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Shangjiong, was granted the title of Prefect; his grandfather, Yong, was Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, promoted to the honorary ranks of Grand Master for Central Service (zhongfeng dafu) and Minister for Correct Governance (zhengzhi qing); his father, Jie, was formerly Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; his principal mother, née Yang, was granted the title of Respectful Lady, and his birth mother was née Zhou; his parents were deceased, his elder brother Weizhen and younger brother Weiyu were Imperial University students, his younger brother Weichi was an Assistant Commander, and his wife was née Liang; he placed fifteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Shi, registered in Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhongfu, and he ranked second in his family. He was thirty-two years old, born on the fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kegong, his grandfather Menglie, and his father Xuan, an Imperial University student. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Xia. His mother alone survived. His elder brother was Zhi. He married née Hao and subsequently née Zhao. He placed sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Shouzhen, registered in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Ziyi, and he ranked second in his family. He was twenty-seven years old, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanhe, his grandfather Bin, and his father Xuan, an Imperial University student. His mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shouyu and his younger brother Shouyue. He married née Kong and subsequently née Liu. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Xixue, registered in Guangshan County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota government-school student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Bozhi, and he ranked first in his family. He was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xu, his grandfather Ming, an annual tribute student, and his father Zhengben. His mother was née Hu. His mother alone survived. His elder brother Xisheng was a Metropolitan Examination graduate (gongshi); his younger brothers were Ximeng, an annual tribute student, Xida, and Xiyi. He married née Lü. He placed thirty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Wen, registered in Qi Subprefecture, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a supplementary student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Zicheng, and he ranked first in his family. He was twenty-eight years old, born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Zongru, and his father Dun. His mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Que. He married née Hu. He placed thirty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Chunfu, courtesy name Xuemu, was registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household; he was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked first in family order, and was aged thirty-three, born on the fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather He, and his father Hu; his mother was née Lin and his stepmother née Huang, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiufu, Yangfu, Kefu, and Defu, and his younger brothers Sanfu, Yuanfu, Chufu, and Lifu; his wife was née Cai. He placed thirty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiong, courtesy name Youming, was registered in Qingping Guard, Guizhou, in an official household, and was originally from Sheng County, Zhejiang; he was a guard-school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ranked seventh in family order, and was aged twenty-four, born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ju was Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, posthumously granted the titles General Who Guards the State and Vice Regional Military Commissioner; his grandfather Zhang was a District Magistrate, honorifically granted the title Investigating Censor; his father Mu was Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, and his mother, née Sun, was granted the title Lady (ruren). He had living parents and grandparents. His elder brothers were Chengzu, a Guard Commander, Xuezu, and Nianzu, and his younger brothers Guan, Lian, and Lang; his wife was née Jin. He placed fifth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Qiao, courtesy name Shinan, was registered in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a salt-producing household; he was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked first in family order, and was aged thirty-four, born on the nineteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Yin, and his father Luan; his mother was née Xu, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji and Dong, and his younger brothers Ke, Jia, He, Gao, Zhi, Bang, and Mu; his wife was née Jia. He placed forty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Kongyang, courtesy name Zizhu, was registered in Wuyi County, Jizhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), in a civilian household; he was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked third in family order, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the second day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Ding, and his father Haoshi, a National University student awaiting selection for office; his mother was née Gao, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kongjia, a National University student, and Konghou, and his younger brother was Kongshi; his wife was née Teng. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

程軏〔貫山東東昌府臨清州民籍，國子生，治易經，字信甫，行二，年三十八，二月初三日生〕。曾祖思忠，祖源，父瑛〔壽官〕，母趙氏。具慶下，兄輗〔七品散官〕，弟輅〔監生〕，娶武氏，繼娶龔氏。山東鄉試第七十五名，會試第二百十七名。
translation_en:
Liu Zhaowen, registered in a military household in Nankang County, Nan’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Rujian; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged twenty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun, his grandfather Enze, and his father Xiang, an annual tribute student; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhaoxun and Zhaoli, and his younger brother was Zhaowu. He married a woman née Tian. He placed thirtieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Cheng, registered in a civilian household in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bangwei; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ding, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Zhang, an honorary official honored for longevity; and his father was Pei, an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Li. His father alone was living. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed eleventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Weizhong, registered in a military household of the Guangning Left Guard in Liaodong and a native of Linqu County, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruwei; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chun. His grandfather Zhen was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director acting as Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue. His father Yu was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and his mother, née Fu, held the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother Weijian and younger brother Weimin were tribute scholars (gongshi); his other younger brothers were Weine, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year, and Weizhi. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed twenty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Yue, registered in a civilian household in Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xinfu; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sizhong, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Ying, an honorary official honored for longevity; his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brother Ni held a seventh-rank prestige title, and his younger brother Lu was a student of the Directorate of Education. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Gong. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Guozhen, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a Confucian scholar. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yining. He ranked twenty-third among his brothers and male cousins, was twenty-six years old, and was born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yande, his grandfather Yupin, his father Kai, and his mother née Mao. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Guochen; his younger brothers were Guoyan, Guobin, Guowang, and Guoqi. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed twenty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tianchong, registered in Mengjin County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zicheng. He ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was twenty-eight years old, and was born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather Feng, his father Ying, and his mother née Chai. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Tianding. He married a woman née Meng. He placed twenty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Sanwei, registered in Changle County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shaoqin. He ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was thirty-eight years old, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in Sichuan; his grandfather was Xian; his father was Shihong, a subprefectural Administrative Assistant. His mother was née Zhao, and his stepmother née Zhang. His father was living, but his mother was deceased. His younger brothers were Sanjin and Sanshan. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed thirtieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Wenxi, registered in Lianjiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Gongjue. He ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Tai, his grandfather Shi, his father Yuan, and his mother née Qiu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Wengang. He married a woman née Su. He placed twenty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zheng Yiluan, courtesy name Mingyang, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-seven, and born on the eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yongkuan, his grandfather Guan, his father Hu, and his mother née Cai; both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Yifeng, and his wife was née Feng. He placed seventy-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Jin, courtesy name Yizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Yichun County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Qiyuan, his grandfather Ai, his father Luan, and his mother née Tang; his father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His younger brothers were Qian, Dao, Yuan, Di, Xun, Yu, and Xuan, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed fifty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Chengqian, courtesy name Deguang, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Jiangyin County. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the fifth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Mengbian, his grandfather Shi, his father Pin, and his mother née Gu; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Song, a prefectural Registrar, Nan, and Zhen; his younger brothers were Cheng, Kai, and Ge. His wife was née Xiao. He placed twenty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Shangwen, courtesy name Zhiqing, was registered in a civilian household in Xincheng County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Haiquan, and his father Da, a county Clerk; his father's former wives were née Qi and née Cui, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Bowen, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed 106th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

蔣宗魯〔貫貴州普安衛軍籍，應天府溧陽縣人，貴州學增廣生，治易經，字道父，行三，年二十，十二月十三日生〕。曾祖銘，祖勝〔義官〕，父廷璧〔南京國子監監正〕，前母徐氏、毛氏，母羅氏。具慶下，兄芹、宗周，弟宗曾，娶潘氏。貴州鄉試第十五名，會試第二百八十名。

李和芳〔貫湖廣荊州府公安縣軍籍，縣學附學生，治書經，字仁父，行二，年三十六，十二月初七日生〕。曾祖謙，祖德明〔八品散官〕，父秀〔監生〕，母嚴氏。永感下，兄文芳〔貢士〕，弟元芳、襲芳、群芳，娶曹氏。湖廣鄉試第四十五名，會試第二百六十九名。

朱徵〔貫河南南陽府唐縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字晉卿，行一，年四十，十月十三日生〕。曾祖文昌，祖寬，父鳳，母劉氏，繼母王氏。永感下，弟德，娶楊氏。河南鄉試第八十名，會試第二百三十名。

黃宗槩〔貫福建福州府閩縣民籍，縣學附學生，治易經，字時節，行九，年三十三，正月十六日生〕。曾祖誠，祖垕慶，父繼魁，母林氏。具慶下，弟裳、宗器〔南京戶部主事〕、宗秩、宗侃、宗偘，娶林氏，繼娶張氏。福建鄉試第五十四名，會試第二百二十名。
translation_en:
Jiang Zonglu 蔣宗魯 was registered in a military household in Pu’an Guard, Guizhou, and was a native of Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture. An added-quota student at the Guizhou school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Daofu; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty years old, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather, Sheng, held the honorary designation of “righteous official”; and his father, Tingbi, was Director [?] of the Nanjing Directorate of Education. His father’s former wives were née Xu and née Mao, and his mother was née Luo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qin and Zongzhou, and his younger brother was Zongzeng. His wife was née Pan. He placed fifteenth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Hefang 李和芳 was registered in a military household in Gong’an County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An attached student at the county school, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Renfu; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian; his grandfather, Deming, held a prestige title of the eighth rank; his father, Xiu, was an Imperial Academy student; and his mother was née Yan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother, Wenfang, was a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Yuanfang, Xifang, and Qunfang. His wife was née Cao. He placed forty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Zheng 朱徵 was registered in a civilian household in Tang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan. An Imperial Academy student, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Jinqing; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenchang; his grandfather was Kuan; his father was Feng; his mother was née Liu; and his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was De, and his wife was née Yang. He placed eightieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zonggai 黃宗槩 was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student at the county school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shijie; he ranked ninth among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather was Houqing; his father was Jikui; and his mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shang, Zongqi, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, Zongzhi, Zongkan 宗侃, and Zongkan 宗偘. His wife was née Lin; he subsequently married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qi Zongdao, courtesy name Shulu, was registered in a military household of Guangning Right Guard in Liaodong and was originally from Rizhao County, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was San; his grandfather, Bin; his father, You, a Registrar; and his mother, née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chun and Zongxian, the latter a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Tai, Zongrui, and Zongzhe. His wife was née Geng. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dao, courtesy name Yunzhong, was registered in an official household of Hengzhou Guard, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ying; his grandfather, Jue, a Company Commander; his father, Xian; and his mother, née Lu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Ben, an Assistant Commander, and Li; his younger brother was Xuan. His wife was née Fan. He placed seventy-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Shou, courtesy name Weiyi, was registered in a civilian household of Shuangliu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites, he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yanhe; his grandfather, Zhi; his father, Tingjian, an Assistant Prefect; his mother, née Wang; and his stepmother, née Shi. Parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Ke and Zhi. His wife was née Ren. He placed fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Shen, courtesy name Boshu, was registered in an artisan household of Le'an County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng; his grandfather, Cong; his father, Yu, an Assistant Magistrate; and his mother, née Zhu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Ji, an Instructor, Lun, and Jin; his younger brothers were Shan and Shou. His wife was née Jiang, and he subsequently married a woman née Cui. He placed forty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Mian 林冕, registered in a civilian household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Duanwu; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Di, his grandfather Tai, his father Xiu, and his mother née He. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xi 㫺 and Hao 昊; his younger brothers were Sheng 昇, Sheng 晟, and Gao 杲. His wife was née Guo. He placed fifty-ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Rui 張瑞, registered in a civilian household in Hui’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yingshi; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty, and was born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongyuan, his grandfather Rongke, his father Kun, and his mother née Sun. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Qi, and his wife was née Huang. He placed forty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Miao Wenlong 繆文龍, registered in a military household of Wusa Guard, Guizhou, and originally from Huating County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Weide; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai, his grandfather Ren, his father Liangyu, a county magistrate, and his mother née Xie. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wenxian and Wenying; his younger brothers were Wenming and Wenfeng. His wife was née Qian. He placed thirty-eighth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ge Tingzhang 葛廷章, registered in an artisan household of the Gongzheng Office 工正所 [?] in Lanzhou, Lintao Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Chaoxian; he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the twenty-second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Zhong, his father Lin, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Tingmei. His wife was née Zhu; he subsequently married a woman née Liu. He placed thirtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Lingyun, registered in Junzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zipeng, ranked third among his brothers, and was aged twenty-six, born on the seventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather, Quan; and his father, Yan, who was granted the title of Investigating Censor. His mother, née Zhou, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chengyun, an Investigating Censor, and Dengyun, a Right Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; his younger brothers were Piyun, Wangyun, Qingyun, and Canyun. His wife was née Shi. He placed tenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Guangpu, registered in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Bogong, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather, Tang; and his father, Xi, a Ceremonial Usher. His mother was née Yu. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Ma. He placed first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xueyi, registered in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household. A National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Daofu, ranked fourth among his brothers, and was aged forty-one, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wengui; his grandfather, Sen; and his father, Yi, a District Magistrate. His mother was née You. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His wife was née Wang. He placed ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Heng, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household. An added-quota student at the prefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Zhizhen, ranked first among his brothers, and was aged twenty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sen, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Rui, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father was Xin. His mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Chen, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.
