黃洪毗〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，府學生，治書經，字協恭，行二，年三十二，八月十六日生〕。曾祖玉英〔贈南京翰林院侍講學士、奉直大夫〕，祖瀾〔南京翰林院侍講學士〕，父肯堂〔貢士〕，母張氏。慈侍下。兄洪崑，弟洪鵬、洪翰、洪化。娶陳氏。福建鄉試第二十二名，會試第四十四名。

周寧〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字彥靖，行七，年四十六，二月二十七日生〕。曾祖勃，祖輔，父仕，母林氏。具慶下。兄宣〔布政使司都事〕、寬、寅，弟密〔聽選官〕、瑞〔知縣〕、完。娶林氏。福建鄉試第三十七名，會試第一百三十六名。
translation_en:
Li Shan, registered in an official household of Hengzhou Guard, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Jingfu, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather was Xian, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was En, and his mother was née Wang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Long, Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; Kui, Commander; Feng; Han; and Qi. His younger brothers were Qiang, Ji, Zhu, and Xu. His wife was née Wang. He placed seventy-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Jiaxiang, registered in a civilian household of Guide Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and originally from Dacang Subprefecture [?], Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Bolin, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Chun, his grandfather was Hong, his father was Shou, and his mother was née Qian. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Qing, and his younger brother was Zai. His wife was née Fan. He placed seventy-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Hongpi, registered in a military household of Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Xiegong, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yuying, posthumously granted the titles of Expositor-in-Waiting of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy and Grand Master for Upright Service; his grandfather was Lan, Expositor-in-Waiting of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy; his father was Kentang, a tribute scholar (gongshi); and his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Hongkun, and his younger brothers were Hongpeng, Honghan, and Honghua. His wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Ning, registered in a military household of Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yanjing, he ranked seventh in birth order, and he was aged forty-six, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Bo, his grandfather was Fu, his father was Shi, and his mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan, Office Manager in a Provincial Administration Commission; Kuan; and Yin. His younger brothers were Mi, an official awaiting selection for appointment; Rui, a County Magistrate; and Wan. His wife was née Lin. He placed thirty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Jing, registered in Cizhou, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Bochang. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty-nine and was born on the sixteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Zhongyou, and his father Guang; his mother was née Ke. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Fu and Xian, and his younger brothers Biao, Jin, and Lun. He married a woman née Li. He ranked fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Ce, registered in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhifu. Third in birth order, he was aged thirty and was born on the ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Puxuan, his grandfather Hong, and his father Quan; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xun and Cai, and his younger brother Hui. He married a woman née Qiu. He ranked eleventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 308th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Meng, registered in Chuzhou in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Duanfu. Fifth in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was He. His grandfather Yungong was a prefectural school instructor. His father Xu was a prefectural judge, received the honorary title of secretary in the Ministry of Rites, and was posthumously granted the title of prefect. His father's former wife, née Li, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Respect; his mother, née Li (黎), received the title Senior Lady of Respect. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Ying, an assistant commander; Xiao, a steward; Zi, an honorary official; Cun, a surveillance vice commissioner; and Ji. His younger brothers were Hou and Fu. He married a woman née Fang. He ranked 133rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yonghe, registered in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural government school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuanle. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-one and was born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Zhan, and his father Jian; his mother was née Han. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yongjing, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Yongzhong. He married a woman née Su. He ranked twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Dai Weishi 戴維師, registered in a salt-producing household in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bingwen; he ranked sixth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-four, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongru; his grandfather was Minju; his father was Guang, a Prefectural Assistant Administrator; and his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Weizhong and Weixiao, and his younger brothers were Weizong, Weizheng, and Weiji. His wife was née Huang. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Xiang 吳相, registered in a commoner household in Neiqiu County, Shunde Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruli; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-five, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Can; his grandfather was Zhen; and his father was Cong. His father's principal wife was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Lü. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His wife was née Gong. He placed forty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Liang 楊梁, registered in a commoner household in Xi'an County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingcai; he ranked seventh among his brothers and male cousins and was aged twenty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Hao, a Judge; his grandfather was Chun, an annual tribute student; his father was Shu; and his mother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tang, and his younger brother was Fei. His wife was née Zheng. He placed twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Qizong 劉起宗, registered in a commoner household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongzhi; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-five, born on the fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Gui, an Investigating Censor, who received successive posthumous honors as Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Supervisor of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent, concurrently a Hanlin Academician, and subsequently as Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Rites. His grandfather was Chun, who directed the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent and held the titles Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Rites, concurrently serving as a Hanlin Academician; he was posthumously appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenjian. His father was Pengnian, a Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and his mother was née Mou, granted the title Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qiyuan, Qidong (an Imperial University student), Qiming, Qimeng, Qijing, Qishen, and Qijiang. His wife was née Li; he subsequently married a woman née Liu 柳. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Sicheng, registered in a civilian household in Gu’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a native of Chang’an County, Shaanxi, and a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zixiu; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Gan, and his father Yongqian; his mothers were Lady Zhang and Lady Xin. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Sijing and Siming, and his younger brothers were Simao, Sirui, and Siyuan. He married Lady Sun and subsequently Lady Wang. He placed thirtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yu, registered in a civilian household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Fanzhi; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Xi was a provincial graduate (juren) who served as acting Instructor; his grandfather was Zhang, his father Yuanzhi, and his mother Lady Lin. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yan, Che, Shu, and Qu. He married Lady Chen. He placed eighty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Huai, registered in a civilian household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was an additional student of the prefectural school specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Yuchuan; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-six, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Xi, his father Tinglan, Director of Foodstuffs, and his mother Lady Xie. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ze, Jin, and Zhu. He married Lady Tian and subsequently Lady Su. He placed nineteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xi, registered in a civilian household in Yongding County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Tinghe; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Shao, his father Shihong, and his mother Lady Zheng. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother Kan was a Medical Instructor, and his younger brother was Jun. He married Lady Lai. He placed ninety-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Bao Daoming, registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Xingzhi; he ranked eighth in family birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Wensu, his father Rongfang, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qing, Lun, Lian, Guang, Shou, Chun, and Long; his younger brothers were Chun, Shen, Qiu, Jian, Xiang, Hong, Tong, Da, Yuan, and Xuan. His wife was née Fang. He placed fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Yuchun, registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and originally from Changshu County, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Tiren; his family birth order is recorded as forty-first [?], and he was born on the twenty-second day of the first month; no age is given. His great-grandfather was Huan (posthumously granted the title of District Magistrate), his grandfather Yong, his father Chong, and his mother née Lu. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brothers were Fuchun, Maochun, and Shouchun; his younger brothers were Fangchun, Cuichun, and Fuchun. His wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Dawu, registered in a civilian household in Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xiangcheng; he ranked first in family birth order and was thirty-one years old, born on the thirtieth day of the intercalary first month. His great-grandfather was Sui, his grandfather Yongning, his father Peng, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Daben, Dazhang, and Dahe. His wife was née Xu; he subsequently married a woman née Li. He placed fifteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Shisi, registered in a military household in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yixue; he ranked twenty-fourth in family birth order and was twenty-five years old, born on the seventeenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Wanyuan, his grandfather Fuchang, his father E (僫) [?], his mother née Wang, and his stepmother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shiming; his younger brothers were Shixiang, Shixing, Shimao, Shiji, Shizhang, Shishi, and Shishi (時軾). His wife was née Zheng. He placed sixty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Dong Zice, courtesy name Yuanzheng, was registered in a military household in Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Jingshan County, Huguang [?; transcribed as 胡廣]. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather, Zhong, held an honorary longevity title; his father was Yue, and his mother was née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Liu. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Zhao, courtesy name Yiming, was registered in a military household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked seventh among his brothers and was aged twenty, born on the nineteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sichu; his grandfather, Jingfa; his father, Shigai; and his mother, née He. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Rujing, Ruliang, Ruyi, and Ruwen, and his wife was née Gu. He placed forty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Chunze, courtesy name Renfu, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Wei, was a prefectural school instructor; his father was Bi, and his mother was née Sheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Xiu, and his wife was née Lin. He placed seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yuanxiang, courtesy name Guozhong, was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boyi; his grandfather, Chun; his father, Long; and his mother, née Xue. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yuanji, Yuanqing, and Yuanzhen; his younger brothers were Yuanzheng, an official awaiting selection for appointment, Yuanbin, Yuanlu, and Yuande. His wife was née Zhou. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 309th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Nie Li, courtesy name Gongshou, was registered in a military household of Linqing Guard, Shandong, and came from Xiangfu County, Henan. A student of the Jining Subprefectural School specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the eleventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather, Min, was an Assistant Instructor; his father, Zan, was an Administrator; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chu, and his younger brother was Ji. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Luosheng, courtesy name Xicheng, was registered in a civilian household of En County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the nineteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather, Jin, was a County Clerk; and his father, Gao, was a County Registrar. His father's former wives were née Ma and née Guo; his mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Lusheng, was an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Chansheng, Minsheng, and Yansheng. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Dashi, courtesy name Zixu, was registered in a civilian household of Queshan County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and came from Zichuan County, Shandong. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather was Jian, his father was Fu, and his mother was née Dong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dazhen and Daguan. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-eighth in both the Henan Provincial Examination and the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Hu, courtesy name Mingxiao, was registered in an official household of Shaoxing Guard, Zhejiang, and came from Wujin County, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the ninth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather, Jie, grandfather, Yi, and father, Rui, were all Company Commanders. His mother, née Li, had been granted the title Lady of Peace (anren). His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother, He, was a Company Commander; his younger brothers were Ming, Feng, and Wu. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Mao. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Binghu, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Guozhen; he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Mian, a student of the Directorate of Education; his grandfather was Daoheng, who held a seventh-rank prestige title; and his father was Chaosheng, a district magistrate. His legal mother was née Weng, and his birth mother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Bingluo, Bingfu, Yingfeng, Tian, and Daji [?]; his younger brothers were Bingchen, Bingqian, and Bingchu. His wife was née Zhu. He placed fourteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wenqing, registered in a military household in Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhifu; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the sixteenth day of the intercalary first month. His great-grandfather was Weixiao, his grandfather was Tong, his father was Zhicong, and his mother was née Shi. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Qinqing and Siqing. His wife was née Du. He placed first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Chuanji, registered in an artisan household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Juqing; he ranked third in birth order and was thirty-four years old, born on the nineteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zongying, his grandfather was Zhenci, and his father was Yan. His mother was née Cheng, and his stepmother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuanheng, Zaijia, and Jiming; his younger brothers were Chengyuan, Penghe, and Wanxing [?]. His wife was née Chen. He placed thirty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Fengming, registered in a military household of the Chenzhou Guard, Huguang, and originating from Xuyi County, Zhili, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zishi; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jing, a company commander; his grandfather was Li, his father was Jing, and his mother was née Yan. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Fengyi. His wife was née Gao. He placed fortieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Lan, courtesy name Qingpei, was registered in a civilian household in Huoshan County, Liu’an Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, and was a National University student associated with Zhanyi Subprefecture, Yunnan. He specialized in the Book of Rites. First in birth order, he was aged forty-four and was born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Tai, was a prefectural-school Professor; and his father, Fengyi, was a School Director. His mother was née Yan. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Chai, and his wife was née Li. He placed 107th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 318th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hao Bin, courtesy name Dabin, was registered in a civilian household in Teng County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, and was a native of Qinghe County in the Metropolitan Region. A National University student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-eight and was born on the sixteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was You, his grandfather was Ming, and his father was Shu. His mother was née Niu, and his stepmother was née Zou. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Ru, and his wife was née Sun. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Liangfu, courtesy name Zibi, was registered in a civilian household in Dongxiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A prefectural-school student, he specialized in the Book of Documents. Twenty-third in birth order, he was aged twenty-four and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lu; his grandfather, Cheng, held an honorary official title for longevity; and his father, Ji, was an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Yue. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Liangqi, and his wife was née Deng. He placed eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang Jian, courtesy name Canke, was registered in a civilian household in Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A National University student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-nine and was born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qianzhen; his grandfather, Tun, held an honorary official title for public beneficence; and his father was Chunxi. His mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lü and Jin, and his wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hong Tinggui, registered in a military household in Nan’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dexin, he ranked third in family birth order, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Minlun; his grandfather, Xin, held a prestige title; his father was Zhou; his mother was née Lin, and his stepmother née Wu. His father was living. His elder brothers were Tingfang, Tingwu, and Tingshi (a tribute student); his younger brothers were Tingxiu and Tinglan. His wife was née Tu. He placed seventy-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Yaochen, registered in a military household in Anju County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bochun, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cunlu; his grandfather was Peng; his father, Ziming, was an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Zhu. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Cheng, and his younger brothers were Shunchen and Yuchen. His wife was née Yang. He placed fiftieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Maozhong, a native of Gaoyang County, Anzhou Subprefecture, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Defu, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was Wen; his father was Bing; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yongzhong, Zhizhong (a District Magistrate), Xunzhong, Bingzhong, Huazhong, and Xinzhong; his younger brothers were Weizhong, Xiezhong, Jizhong, Longzhong, Lüzhong, Jiuzhong, and Shizhong. His wife was née Yuan. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Weiqing, registered in an artisan household of the Wugong Central Guard and a native of Kunshan County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an attached student of the Shuntian prefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yinzhong, he ranked first in family birth order, and he was aged thirty, born on the second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fujing; his grandfather was Tai; his father was Sheng; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Weihe and Weiyi. His wife was née Wen. He placed 106th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

孟顏〔貫山西澤州民籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字學顏，行一，年二十四，三月初一日生〕。曾祖彪〔贈太僕寺少卿，加贈都察院右副都御史〕，祖春〔通議大夫，吏部左侍郎〕，父陽〔行人，贈監察御史〕，母顏氏〔封孺人〕。永感下，弟學孔、學思、顓、頊、學堯，娶龐氏。山西鄉試第三名，會試第一百九十一名。
translation_en:
Ni Yuan, courtesy name Gongyin, was registered in a civilian household in Xianning County, Shaanxi, and was a native of Changzhou County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was fourth in family order, aged thirty-five, and born on the eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shu; his grandfather, Hao, held a prestige title; and his father, Tong, was granted the title of Supervising Secretary. His father's principal wife, née Liu, was granted the title of Lady (ruren); his birth mother was also née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Ji, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; Huan, Station Master; Dai, a tribute scholar; Yao; and Pei. His younger brother Huang was an Imperial University student. His wife was née Huang. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Gun, courtesy name Buzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in family order, aged forty, and born on the sixteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Cong; his grandfather was Jing; his father, Zi, was a Subprefect; and his mother was née Han. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Biao, Vice Commander in a Nanjing Wardens' Office, and Jiong. His younger brothers were Bao, an Imperial University student; Zhi, a tribute scholar; and Qiu. His wife was née Lu. He placed sixty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhuang Sikuan, courtesy name Junli, was registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in family order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yize; his grandfather was Yuanshan; his father was Long; and his mother was née Guo. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Sigong, and his younger brother was Sixin. His wife was née Zhang. He placed sixty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Yan, courtesy name Xueyan, was registered in a civilian household in Zezhou, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in family order, aged twenty-four, and born on the first day of the third month. His great-grandfather, Biao, was posthumously granted the title of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and subsequently that of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather, Chun, was Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Left Vice Minister of Personnel. His father, Yang, was a Messenger, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his mother, née Yan, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Xuekong, Xuesi, Zhuan, Xu, and Xueyao. His wife was née Pang. He placed third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

趙之屏〔貫四川順慶府南充縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字憲甫，行一，年二十八，十二月十四日生〕。曾祖永富，祖廷爵，父愷，母師氏。具慶下，弟之翰、之藩、之綱、之紀，娶韓氏。四川鄉試第七名，會試第一百四十五名。

甄成德〔貫山西太原府平定州守禦千戶所軍籍，攸縣國子生，治書經，字行叔，行一，年三十八，七月初四日生〕。曾祖海，祖福祥，父鏞，母郭氏。具慶下，弟成業、成性、成仁、成義，娶馬氏。山西鄉試第三十八名，會試第二百五十一名。

冷珂〔貫四川重慶府榮昌縣軍籍，湖廣麻城縣人，國子生，治易經，字鳴叔，行五，年四十，六月二十日生〕。曾祖廷傑，祖奎〔敎諭，贈奉政大夫、府同知〕，父宗元〔知府〕，母張氏〔贈宜人〕，繼母鄭氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下。四川鄉試第五十九名，會試第一百四十名。
translation_en:
Liu Qian 劉乾, registered in a military household in Tang County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhongkun; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the eleventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhu, a county school instructor; his grandfather was Yu, an examining editor in the Hanlin Academy; his father was Rujiao, and his mother was née Zuo. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Ding and Tai, and his younger brother was Heng. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Xu. He placed 117th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Zhiping 趙之屏, registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xianfu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yongfu, his grandfather Tingjue, his father Kai, and his mother née Shi. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhihan, Zhifan, Zhigang, and Zhiji. He married a woman née Han. He placed seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhen Chengde 甄成德, registered in a military household of the Defense Battalion of Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education associated with You County [?] who specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Xingshu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather Fuxiang, his father Yong, and his mother née Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chengye, Chengxing, Chengren, and Chengyi. He married a woman née Ma. He placed 38th in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Leng Ke 冷珂, registered in a military household in Rongchang County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, and a native of Macheng County, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Mingshu; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Tingjie; his grandfather was Kui, a county school instructor posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Governance and the office of prefectural vice prefect; his father was Zongyuan, a prefect. His mother, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother, née Zheng, was granted the same title. His father and stepmother were living. He placed 59th in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Meng Tingxiang, courtesy name Yuanli, was registered in a military household in Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twelfth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was An, a prefectural Records Examiner; his grandfather was Qin, a holder of a seventh-rank prestige title; his father was Ying, a subprefectural school Instructor; and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tingfang and Tinglin, and his wife was née Si. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xuan, courtesy name Ziquan, was registered in a civilian household in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and was a native of Anyi County, Shanxi. A student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the sixteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shun, his grandfather was Jiang, and his father was Liang; his legal mother was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Zheng. He placed second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shangxue, courtesy name Minshu, was registered in a civilian household in Maping County, Liuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the eleventh day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather was Su, his father was Xiang, and his mother was née Wen. Both parents were living. His wife was née Chen. He placed third in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang De, courtesy name Ruxiu, was registered in a military salt-producing household in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-one, and born on the twelfth day of the intercalary twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingfang, his grandfather was Juan, his father was Yi, and his mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qing and Li, and his wife was née Shao. He placed eightieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

謝體升〔貫江西吉安府吉水縣軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字順之，行五，年三十三，三月二十五日生〕。曾祖建康，祖克選〔義官〕，父顯〔禮部儒士〕，前母高氏，母蕭氏，繼母周氏。具慶下，兄體蒙〔監生〕、體師、體鼎〔監生〕，弟體復，娶黃氏。江西鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百二十七名。

唐時〔貫直隸保定府雄縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字學孔，行一，年二十七，十月二十二日生〕。曾祖興，祖全，父林，母高氏。具慶下，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十一名，會試第四十一名。

魏謙吉〔貫直隸真定府栢鄉縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字子惠，行四，年三十，十一月初一日生〕。曾祖鑑，祖壽〔訓導〕，父巖〔儒官〕，母趙氏。具慶下，兄謙光〔監生〕、謙亨、謙利，弟謙貞、謙榮、謙勞、謙撝，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第二名，會試第五名。

張情〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字約之，行二，年三十六，九月二十四日生〕。曾祖思明，祖繪，父祥〔歲貢生〕，母杜氏。慈侍下，兄性，弟意〔按察司副使〕、心，娶朱氏。應天府鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百一名。
translation_en:
Xie Tisheng, courtesy name Shunzhi, was registered in a military household in Jishui County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiankang; his grandfather was Kexuan, an honorary official for public benefaction; and his father was Xian, a Confucian scholar attached to the Ministry of Rites. His father's former wife was née Gao, his mother née Xiao, and his stepmother née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Timeng, an Imperial University student, Tishi, and Tiding, also an Imperial University student; his younger brother was Tifu. His wife was née Huang. He ranked fifty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Shi, courtesy name Xuekong, was registered in a civilian household in Xiong County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Quan, his father Lin, and his mother née Gao. Both parents were living. His wife was née Li. He ranked 121st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Qianji, courtesy name Zihui, was registered in a civilian household in Baixiang County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather was Shou, an Assistant Instructor; his father was Yan, an educational official; and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qianguang, an Imperial University student, Qianheng, and Qianli; his younger brothers were Qianzhen, Qianrong, Qianlao, and Qianhui. His wife was née Li. He ranked second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qing, courtesy name Yuezhi, was registered in an artisan household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siming, his grandfather Hui, his father Xiang, an annual tribute student, and his mother née Du. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Xing; his younger brothers were Yi, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Xin. His wife was née Zhu. He ranked forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

查秉彝〔貫浙江杭州府海寧縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字性甫，行八，年三十五，四月十三日生〕。曾祖實，祖益〔封按察司僉事〕，父繪，母周氏。永感下，兄秉中、秉直、秉衡、秉清、秉濂、秉銓〔監生〕，弟秉鉞〔貢士〕、秉倫、秉信、秉佶、秉鈞，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第二十一名，會試第十五名。

吳世良〔貫浙江嚴州府遂安縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字元良，行三，年三十，十一月十三日生〕。曾祖汝廣，祖士雍〔壽官〕，父漢，母余氏。具慶下，兄世恩、世忠，弟世義、宗魯，娶凌氏，繼娶嚴氏。浙江鄉試第九名，會試第一百六十名。

張詔〔貫山東濟南府濟陽縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字朝宣，行一，年二十八，三月初六日生〕。曾祖斌，祖玉，父遵，前母劉氏，母周氏。嚴侍下，弟侶、儔、化、儒，娶謝氏，繼娶謝氏。山東鄉試第三十五名，會試第一百六十九名。
translation_en:
Liu Tao, registered in a military household of Tianjin Left Guard in Zhili and originally from Xiangcheng County, Henan, was a guard-school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Renfu, he ranked third in his family, and he was twenty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Qing, and his father Qi, who held an honorary title for longevity; his mother was née Shi, both parents were living, his elder brothers were Xun and Chen, and his wife was née Chen; he placed forty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zha Bingyi, registered in a civilian household of Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xingfu, he ranked eighth in his family, and he was thirty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Shi, his grandfather Yi, who had been honorifically appointed Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, and his father Hui; his mother was née Zhou, both parents were deceased, his elder brothers were Bingzhong, Bingzhi, Bingheng, Bingqing, Binglian, and Bingquan (a student of the Directorate of Education), his younger brothers were Bingyue (a Metropolitan Examination graduate), Binglun, Bingxin, Bingji, and Bingjun, and his wife was née Chen; he placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shiliang, registered in a civilian household of Sui'an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county-school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yuanliang, he ranked third in his family, and he was thirty, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ruguang, his grandfather Shiyong, who held an honorary title for longevity, and his father Han; his mother was née Yu, both parents were living, his elder brothers were Shien and Shizhong, his younger brothers were Shiyi and Zonglu, and he married a woman née Ling and subsequently a woman née Yan; he placed ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhao, registered in a civilian household of Jiyang County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was a county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Chaoxuan, he ranked first in his family, and he was twenty-eight, born on the sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Yu, and his father Zun; his father's former wife was née Liu and his mother was née Zhou, his father was living and his mother deceased, his younger brothers were Lü, Chou, Hua, and Ru, and he married a woman née Xie and subsequently another woman née Xie; he placed thirty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qiu Dai, courtesy name Wenyu, was from Liu'an Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and belonged to a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Song, his grandfather Xuan, his father Fu, and his mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Heng and his younger brother Rui. He married a woman née Gong and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed 109th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shi, courtesy name Youhua, was from Lingbao County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, and belonged to a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zi, an Honorary Official for Philanthropy; his grandfather was Mengyang, his father Yin, and his mother née Ge. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiyi and Jiru, and his younger brother was Shou. He married a woman née Yan. He placed 74th in the Henan Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Xuan, courtesy name Bowen, was from Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and belonged to an artisan household. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Shunqian, his grandfather Chenggao, his father Yuanming, and his mother née Zheng. His father had died, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brother was Lin and his younger brother Jing. He married a woman née Xiao. He placed 83rd in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 288th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qian, courtesy name Shijian, was from Qihe County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, and belonged to an official household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-two, born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather was Juren, a Transport Commissioner; his father was Jiujing; and his mother was née Bi. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Jin, Jiong, Yang, Lai, Xiang, and Zhan. He was betrothed to a woman née Li. He placed 32nd in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

曾祖寧 祖玘 父謐〔知縣〕 母茅氏

黃如桂〔貫江西吉安府廬陵縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字德馨，行三，年四十二，三月十二日生〕。曾祖時佐，祖鎬，父懋哲，母李氏。永感下，兄照、文、喬，娶李氏。江西鄉試第八名，會試第十九名。

蕭世延〔貫四川成都府內江縣，民籍，縣學生，治書經，字可靜，行六，年三十四，四月初十日生〕。曾祖汝明〔贈都察院右都御史〕，祖騏〔義官〕，父露，嫡母吳氏，生母李氏。慈侍下，兄世顯〔壽官〕、世雍、世選、世範〔監生〕、世建，弟世蒿、世萱、世塤、世謙、世賞，娶毛氏，繼娶冷氏。四川鄉試第十名，會試第三百十一名。

羅廷繡〔貫陝西西安府邠州淳化縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字公裳，行七，年三十，閏九月初八日生〕。曾祖楫〔知州〕，祖九霄〔壽官〕，父仁夫，母袁氏。重慶下，弟廷紱，娶姚氏。陝西鄉試第五十二名，會試第三百七名。

金志〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字允立，行六十一，年三十七，三月十三日生〕。曾祖寧，祖玘，父謐〔知縣〕，母茅氏。永感下，兄恕、愚，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第六十名，會試第二百八名。
translation_en:
Huang Rugui, registered in Luling County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Dexin; he ranked third in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the twelfth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Shizuo, his grandfather Gao, his father Maozhe, and his mother née Li. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhao, Wen, and Qiao; his wife was née Li. He placed eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Shiyan, registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Kejing; he ranked sixth in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ruming, posthumously appointed Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather was Qi, an honorary official recognized for public beneficence; and his father was Lu. His legal mother was née Wu, and his birth mother née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Shixian, an honorary official recognized for longevity; Shiyong; Shixuan; Shifan, a student of the Directorate of Education; and Shijian. His younger brothers were Shihao, Shixuan, Shixun, Shiqian, and Shishang. He married a woman née Mao and subsequently a woman née Leng. He placed tenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 311th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Tingxiu, registered in Chunhua County, Binzhou, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Gongshang; he ranked seventh in his family and was aged thirty, born on the eighth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ji, a department magistrate; his grandfather was Jiuxiao, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Renfu; and his mother was née Yuan. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Tingfu, and his wife was née Yao. He placed fifty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 307th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Zhi, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yunli; he ranked sixty-first in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Ning, his grandfather Qi, his father Mi, a district magistrate, and his mother née Mao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shu and Yu; his wife was née Chen. He placed sixtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
余善繼，貫四川重慶府長壽縣，民籍，縣學附學生，治春秋，字伯賢，行一，年二十七，三月初三日生。曾祖永壽，祖鍾〔王府教授〕，父龍，母趙氏。具慶下，兄廷寵，弟能繼、可繼，娶謝氏。四川鄉試第三十一名，會試第二百十名。

吳道南，貫河南汝寧府光州，民籍，江西豐城縣人，國子生，治易經，字文在，行二，年三十一，八月十二日生。曾祖世榮，祖權，父昭鳳，母金氏，繼母陳氏。具慶下，弟道明，娶蔡氏。河南鄉試第五十八名，會試第六十七名。

楊載鳴，貫江西吉安府泰和縣，儒籍，縣學生，治易經，字虛卿，行二，年二十五，十二月二十三日生。曾祖昱〔太僕寺丞〕，祖雯，父訓〔教諭〕，母劉氏。具慶下，兄載芳，弟載賞，娶龍氏。江西鄉試第十五名，會試第一百名。

沈鍊，貫浙江紹興衛，軍籍，麗水縣人，國子生，治易經，字純甫，行五，年三十二，九月初八日生。曾祖伯才，祖慶，父璧，母俞氏。具慶下，兄鎮、鎧、釧，弟鎬、鍾、鈇、鎰、鍔，娶徐氏。浙江鄉試第六十五名，會試第一百七名。
translation_en:
Yu Shanji, registered in Changshou County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, in the civilian register, was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Boxian, and he ranked first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongshou; his grandfather was Zhong (Professor in a princely establishment); his father was Long, and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tingchong, and his younger brothers were Nengji and Keji; his wife was née Xie. He placed thirty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Daonan, registered in Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, in the civilian register, was a native of Fengcheng County, Jiangxi, and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Wenzai, and he ranked second in birth order, aged thirty-one, born on the twelfth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shirong; his grandfather was Quan; his father was Zhaofeng, his mother was née Jin, and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Daoming; his wife was née Cai. He placed fifty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zaiming, registered in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in the scholar register, was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xuqing, and he ranked second in birth order, aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu (Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud); his grandfather was Wen; his father was Xun (Instructor), and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zaifang, and his younger brother was Zaishang; his wife was née Long. He placed fifteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 100th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Lian, registered in Shaoxing Guard, Zhejiang, in the military register, was a native of Lishui County and a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Chunfu, and he ranked fifth in birth order, aged thirty-two, born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bocai; his grandfather was Qing; his father was Bi, and his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhen, Kai, and Chuan, and his younger brothers were Hao, Zhong, Fu, Yi, and E; his wife was née Xu. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李一瀚〔貫浙江台州府僊居縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字源甫，行四，年三十四，八月二十日生〕。曾祖良平，祖震，父鑵，母彭氏。具慶下，兄一灌、一浙、一潮，弟一沛，娶應氏。浙江鄉試第八十六名，會試第六十四名。

洪恩〔貫湖廣黃州府蘄州黃梅縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字從仁，行一，年二十九，十月十四日生〕。曾祖宇璇，祖晟〔知縣〕，父模〔貢士〕，母胡氏。重慶下，弟勳、逵、造，娶王氏。湖廣鄉試第三十六名，會試第四十七名。

符驗〔貫浙江台州府黃巖縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字大克，行亨六十八，年四十六，八月十四日生〕。曾祖永廉，祖孚，父匡〔教諭〕，母金氏。永感下，兄璽，弟瓊，娶王氏，繼娶吳氏。浙江鄉試第七名，會試第八十八名。

高謙〔貫陝西綏德衛軍籍，榆林衛人，國子生，治春秋，字孔益，行五，年三十六，七月十八日生〕。曾祖旺，祖英〔百戶〕，父鸞〔府經歷〕，前母王氏，母張氏。慈侍下，兄奎〔百戶〕、儒〔千戶〕、科、第，娶時氏。陝西鄉試第四十六名，會試第二百三十九名。
translation_en:
Li Yihan 李一瀚 was registered in a civilian household in Xianju County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanfu, and he ranked fourth among his brothers. He was thirty-four years old, born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Liangping, his grandfather Zhen, his father Guan, and his mother née Peng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yiguan, Yizhe, and Yichao; his younger brother was Yipei. He married a woman née Ying. He placed eighty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hong En 洪恩 was registered in a civilian household in Huangmei County, Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A county school student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Congren, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-nine years old, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yuxuan; his grandfather Sheng was a District Magistrate; his father Mo was a tribute student; and his mother was née Hu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Xun, Kui, and Zao. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Yan 符驗 was registered in a military household in Huangyan County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Dake; his family seniority is recorded as “heng, sixty-eight” [?]. He was forty-six years old, born on the fourteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yonglian, his grandfather Fu, his father Kuang, a county Confucian School Instructor, and his mother née Jin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xi, and his younger brother Qiong. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Qian 高謙 was registered in a military household of Suide Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Yulin Guard. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Kongyi, and he ranked fifth among his brothers. He was thirty-six years old, born on the eighteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather Ying was a Company Commander; and his father Luan was a prefectural Office Manager. His father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Kui, a Company Commander; Ru, a Battalion Commander; Ke; and Di. He married a woman née Shi. He placed forty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳維嶽〔貫浙江湖州府安吉州孝豐縣軍籍，縣學生，治禮記，字峻伯，行五，年二十五，六月初四日生〕。曾祖玘〔壽官〕，祖松〔封奉政大夫吏部郎中〕，父麟〔知縣，前監察御史〕，前母王氏〔贈孺人〕、王氏，母方氏〔封孺人〕。重慶下，弟維川、維夏、維京、維城，娶臧氏。浙江鄉試第五名，會試第一百九十七名。

萬虞愷〔貫江西南昌府南昌縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字懋卿，行九，年三十四，三月十三日生〕。曾祖景星，祖必昌，父廣載，母傅氏，繼母李氏。具慶下，兄虞託、虞詩，弟虞瑞、虞鄰，娶蕭氏。江西鄉試第八十六名，會試第一百三十九名。

茅坤〔貫浙江湖州府歸安縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字順甫，行二，年二十七，七月二十一日生〕。曾祖剛，祖珪，父遷，母李氏。重慶下，兄乾，弟艮、益、應龍、大有、應虎，娶姚氏。浙江鄉試第十一名，會試第十三名。
translation_en:
Ru Qixian, registered in a civilian household in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Maosi; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Sicong, a Commander in a Wardens' Office; his grandfather was Zhongqi, posthumously appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel; and his father was Tai, a Prefect. His father's former wife, née Yu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his mother, née Ding, was granted the same title. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Weixian, a Subprefectural Assistant Judge, Gong, and Zhi. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fifty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Weiyue, registered in a military household in Xiaofeng County, Anji Subprefecture, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county government student specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Junbo; he ranked fifth in his family and was aged twenty-five, born on the fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Qi, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Song, honorifically appointed Grand Master for Administration and Director in the Ministry of Personnel; and his father was Lin, a District Magistrate and formerly an Investigating Censor. His father's former wives were both née Wang, the first posthumously granted the title Lady for Service; his mother, née Fang, was granted that title. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Weichuan, Weixia, Weijing, and Weicheng. He married a woman née Zang. He placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wan Yukai, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Maoqing; he ranked ninth in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Jingxing, his grandfather Bichang, and his father Guangzai. His mother was née Fu and his stepmother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yutuo and Yushi; his younger brothers were Yurui and Yulin. He married a woman née Xiao. He placed eighty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Kun, registered in a civilian household in Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county government student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Shunfu; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Gang, his grandfather Gui, and his father Qian; his mother was née Li. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Qian; his younger brothers were Gen, Yi, Yinglong, Dayou, and Yinghu. He married a woman née Yao. He placed eleventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
汪宗伊〔貫湖廣武昌府崇陽縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字子衡，行三，年二十九，正月十五日生〕。曾祖璉〔壽官〕，祖藻〔監生，封兵部主事，贈中憲大夫、都察院右僉都御史〕，父文盛〔都察院右僉都御史〕，母彭氏〔封恭人〕。具慶下，兄宗元〔禮部主事〕、宗凱〔中書舍人〕、宗皐，弟宗尹〔貢士〕、宗黎、宗南、宗光、宗太、宗栻、宗記、宗正，娶蔡氏。湖廣鄉試第一名，會試第二十三名。

馮璋〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣，軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字如之，行六十七，年三十七，七月十四日生〕。曾祖民，祖魯，父偁，前母張氏，母魏氏。慈侍下，兄禮、良、貴、岳〔知府〕，弟節，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第三十八名，會試第九名。

林紳〔貫陝西鳳翔府寶鷄縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字佩之，行六，年四十七，九月十三日生〕。曾祖秀，祖虎〔贈知州〕，父恭〔知府〕，嫡母焦氏〔封恭人〕，生母張氏。永感下，兄經〔義官〕、綸〔監生〕、繼〔監生〕、緒〔監生〕、純，弟綽〔上林苑監錄事〕，娶彭氏。陝西鄉試第三十九名，會試第二百七十名。

順境〔貫湖廣武昌府江夏縣，軍籍，府學生，治詩經，字履常，行三，年三十八，四月十五日生〕。曾祖德昭，祖成美，父友剛，母順氏。慈侍下，兄鉉、錫，娶郝氏。湖廣鄉試第四十四名，會試第五十六名。
translation_en:
Wang Zongyi, registered in Chongyang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Ziheng; he ranked third in his family and was twenty-nine years old, born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lian, an honorary official for longevity; his grandfather was Zao, an Imperial University student, granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of War and posthumously awarded the titles of Grand Master for Constitutional Service and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father was Wensheng, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his mother, née Peng, was granted the title Lady of Respect. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zongyuan, Secretary in the Ministry of Rites; Zongkai, a Central Secretariat Drafter; and Zonggao. His younger brothers were Zongyin, a Metropolitan Examination graduate (gongshi); Zongli; Zongnan; Zongguang; Zongtai; Zongshi; Zongji; and Zongzheng. He married a woman née Cai. He placed first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Zhang, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Ruzhi; he ranked sixty-seventh in his family and was thirty-seven years old, born on the fourteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min, his grandfather was Lu, and his father was Cheng. His father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Wei. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Li, Liang, Gui, and Yue, the last a Prefect; his younger brother was Jie. He married a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Shen, registered in Baoji County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Peizhi; he ranked sixth in his family and was forty-seven years old, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiu; his grandfather was Hu, posthumously awarded the title of Subprefect; and his father was Gong, a Prefect. His legal mother, née Jiao, was granted the title Lady of Respect; his birth mother was née Zhang. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jing, an honorary official for charitable service; Lun, Ji, and Xu, all Imperial University students; and Chun. His younger brother was Chuo, a Recorder in the Directorate of Imperial Parks. He married a woman née Peng. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shun Jing, registered in Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Lüchang; he ranked third in his family and was thirty-eight years old, born on the fifteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dezhao, his grandfather was Chengmei, his father was Yougang, and his mother was née Shun. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Xuan and Xi. He married a woman née Hao. He placed forty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

李槃〔貫湖廣岳州府澧州官籍，四川内江縣人，國子生，治易經，字新甫，行三，年三十六，十二月初六日生〕。曾祖蕃〔兵科左給事中，累贈資政大夫、太子少保、工部尚書兼都察院左副都御史〕，祖充嗣〔工部尚書兼都察院左副都御史，贈資政大夫、太子少保〕，父振詞，前母馬氏，母程氏。永感下，兄檯、棠〔同知〕、幹〔千戶〕、弁〔百戶〕，弟熙、松〔光祿寺署丞〕。娶張氏，繼娶陳氏。湖廣鄉試第二名，會試第一百十九名。

阮高〔貫直隸保定府大寧都司官籍，中衛人，國子生，治詩經，字思抑，行二，年二十九，二月初一日生〕。曾祖璿〔都指揮使〕，祖洪，父泰，母李氏。慈侍下，兄登。娶李氏，繼娶尹氏。順天府鄉試第十一名，會試第二百二十九名。
translation_en:
Li Pan 李槃, courtesy name Xinfu, was registered in an official household in Lizhou, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, and was a native of Neijiang County, Sichuan. A National University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty-six, born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Fan was Left Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War and received successive posthumous honors as Grand Master for Aid in Governance, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Works concurrently serving as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather Chongsi was Minister of Works concurrently serving as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent. His father was Zhenci; his father's former wife was née Ma, and his mother was née Cheng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tai, Tang (Vice Prefect), Gan (Battalion Commander), and Bian (Company Commander); his younger brothers were Xi and Song (Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments). He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Song 李嵩, courtesy name Zizhong, was registered in a military household of Guide Guard, Henan, and was a native of Huayin County, Shaanxi. An additional-quota student of the Guide Subprefectural School specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second in birth order and was aged twenty-two, born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Tong, and his father Fang; his mother was née Song and his stepmother née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Kun. He married a woman née Chen. He placed seventeenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Cunde 劉存德, courtesy name Zhiren, was registered in a civilian household in Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-one, born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hongyuan, his grandfather Chaoquan, and his father Gong; his mother was née Ye and his stepmother née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Cunye. He married a woman née Ye. He placed forty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ruan Gao 阮高, courtesy name Siyi, was registered in an official household of the Daning Regional Military Commission in Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, and was a native of Zhongwei (Central Guard). A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Xuan was Regional Military Commissioner; his grandfather was Hong, his father Tai, and his mother née Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Deng. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Yin. He placed eleventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

盛唐〔貫浙江嘉興府嘉善縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字原陶，行一，三十，十一月十五日生〕。曾祖完，祖莊，父奎，母沈氏。具慶下，弟虞，娶戴氏。浙江鄉試第六十名，會試第九十八名。

translation_en:
You Zhende, registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruqian; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty, born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingkuan, who held an honorary longevity title; his grandfather was Kan; and his father was Taiheng. His father's former wife was née Cheng, and his mother was née Wang. His mother alone survived. His elder brother was Mengde, and his younger brothers were Zaide, Sande, Zhuangde, Tongde, Mingde, and Houde. His wife was née Zhan. He placed eighty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Ruzhen, registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Gongning; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-six, born on the seventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming, a prefectural Registrar; his grandfather was Hua, an Administrator; and his father was Chun, a prefectural Assistant Prefect. His mother was née Ren. Both parents survived. His elder brothers were Gan, Ruji, Mian, Han, and Jun; his younger brothers were Gao and Rugan. His wife was née Yang, and his subsequent wife was née Liao. He placed forty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Tang, registered in a civilian household in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuantao; he ranked first in his family and was aged thirty, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wan; his grandfather was Zhuang; his father was Kui; and his mother was née Shen. Both parents survived. His younger brother was Yu, and his wife was née Dai. He placed sixtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yuchun, registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a native of Wu County and a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shifang; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong; his grandfather was Geng; his father was Qian; and his mother was née Hang. Both parents survived. His elder brothers were Yingchun, a sacrificial attendant (shengjiguan), and Xiuchun. His wife was née Jiang. He placed eighty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zheng Zhi, courtesy name Zijing, was registered in a military household in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers, was twenty-eight years old, and was born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Guan, a Judicial Supervisor in a Provincial Administration Commission, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Lun; and his father was Weiyuan, an Assistant Prefect. His mother was née Li, and his stepmother née Liang. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Li, an Imperial University student, and Shi, Jian, Tong, and Deng. His wife was née Xu. He placed thirtieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hang Jinliang [?; surname transcribed as 吭], courtesy name Rushuai, was registered in a civilian household in Ansu County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was Instructor at the county school of Anyi, Shanxi, and specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked third among his brothers, was forty-four years old, and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Gong; his grandfather was Feng; his father was Dagang, a County Registrar; and his mother was née Yan. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jinxian and Jinshan, and his younger brothers were Jinchen, Jinyan, Jindao, and Jinyou. His wife was née Li; his subsequent wives were née Guo, Li, and Wang. He placed ninety-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 312th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Weine, courtesy name Ruyan, was registered in a military household of Guangning Left Guard, Liaodong, and was a native of Linqu County, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fifth among his brothers, was twenty-six years old, and was born on the nineteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather was Zhen, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director acting as Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; and his father was Yu, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His mother, née Fu, was granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Weijian, a tribute scholar; Weizhong, a metropolitan graduate of the same examination year; and Weimin, a tribute scholar. His younger brother was Weizhi, and his wife was née Xiong. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Dongwang, courtesy name Yinglu, was registered in a banner household of Pingshan Guard, Shandong, and was a native of Susong County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fifth among his brothers, was thirty years old, and was born on the first day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Hong, posthumously granted the title of District Magistrate; his grandfather was Hui, an Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; his father was Yao, a Ceremonial Usher; and his mother was née Tian. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Dongming, a County Registrar; Donggao, an Imperial University student; Dongshu, a student admitted by virtue of an official's privilege; Dongying, an Imperial University student; and Donghua, a Company Commander. His younger brothers were Dongju; Dongzuo, an honorary official for charitable contributions; Dongjian; and Dongguang, also an honorary official for charitable contributions. His wife was née Shen. He placed forty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.
