translation_en:
Zhou Nan, registered in the guardsman category of the Ceremonial Guard Office of Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenhua; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Shiyuan, his grandfather Fuhao, and his father Yu; his mother was née Pan. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dunren, of civilian registration in Lishui County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhong’an; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the tenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Wenbing; his grandfather Ning was an Assistant Instructor, and his father Qin was an Instructor. His mother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Dunhou; his younger brothers were Dunhua and Dunfu, the latter a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Pan. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Huan, of civilian registration in Shanyang County, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yanghui; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Gui; his mother was née Ye. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Can and Xun; his younger brothers were Bing and Gao. He married a woman née Liu. He placed sixty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Nan Fengji, of military registration in Weinan County, Huazhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanzhen; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-five, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yan, and his grandfather Gui. His father Jin was an Instructor, additionally awarded posthumously the titles of Grand Master for Governance and Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His mother, née Jiao, was additionally granted the title of Senior Lady of Suitability. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Daji was a Prefect. He married a woman née Li. He placed third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

呂顒〔貫陝西慶陽府寧州，民籍，國子生，治《書經》，字幼誠，行二，年三十六，四月二十六日生〕。曾祖英〔州判官〕，祖昇〔贈徵仕郎、禮科給事中〕，父經〔前都察院右副都御史〕，母高氏〔封孺人〕。嚴侍下，兄顓〔知府〕，弟頎、碩、預，娶周氏。陝西鄉試第七名，會試第八十九名。

辛烜然〔貫山西太原府石州，軍籍，州學生，治《易經》，字養晦，行二，年二十九，十一月初十日生〕。曾祖憲，祖文淵〔知府〕，父柱〔府通判〕，母張氏〔贈孺人〕，繼母郝氏〔封孺人〕。具慶下，兄煜然，弟熺然、爚然，娶溫氏。山西鄉試第四十六名，會試第一百三十名。

徐楚〔貫浙江嚴州府淳安縣，民籍，國子生，治《春秋》，字世望，行一，年三十七，七月初一日生〕。曾祖恒，祖源，父讓，母王氏。慈侍下，弟懋、棼，娶盧氏，繼娶洪氏。浙江鄉試第八十四名，會試第十七名。

蔣坎〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣，軍籍，縣學附學生，治《易經》，字養孚，行十一，年三十二，十二月二十七日生〕。曾祖寧，祖𨞬，父栻，母劉氏。具慶下，兄坤、臨、達善、鼎、渙、泰、師，娶黃氏。浙江鄉試第八十二名，會試第一百四十七名。
translation_en:
Lü Yong 呂顒, registered in Ningzhou, Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Youcheng. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, a subprefectural assistant magistrate; his grandfather was Sheng, posthumously granted the titles Gentleman for Rendering Service and Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites; his father was Jing, formerly Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate. His mother, née Gao, was granted the title Lady (ruren). His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His elder brother was Zhuan, a prefect; his younger brothers were Qi, Shuo, and Yu. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xin Xuanran 辛烜然, registered in Shizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yanghui. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and was born on the tenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather was Wenyuan, a prefect; his father was Zhu, an assistant prefect. His mother, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); his stepmother, née Hao, was granted the same title. His father and stepmother were both living. His elder brother was Yuran; his younger brothers were Xiran and Yueran. He married a woman née Wen. He placed forty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Chu 徐楚, registered in Chun’an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shiwang. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng; his grandfather was Yuan; his father was Rang; his mother was née Wang. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His younger brothers were Mao and Fen. He married a woman née Lu and subsequently a woman née Hong. He placed eighty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Kan 蔣坎, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was an attached student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yangfu. Eleventh in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ning; his grandfather’s name is transcribed as 𨞬 [?]; his father was Shi; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kun, Lin, Dashan [?], Ding, Huan, Tai, and Shi. He married a woman née Huang. He placed eighty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

盛若林〔貫廣東潮州府海陽縣軍籍，府學生，治詩經，字子才，行一，年三十，十一月二十六日生〕。曾祖鳳儀〔教諭，贈奉政大夫、左春坊左庶子兼翰林院侍讀〕，祖端明〔都察院右副都御史〕，父瀚〔歲貢監生〕，母陸氏。重慶下，弟若樹〔貢士〕、若植、若楙、若窠、若枚，娶翁氏。廣東鄉試第二十二名，會試第二百九十二名。

translation_en:
Zhao Tongyan, registered in a military household in Changqing County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Defu, he ranked second in birth order, and he was twenty-two, born on the nineteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather was Ming, a Police Chief; his father was Jianzhi, an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tongren, and his younger brothers were Tongxiang, Tongxian, Tongcai, and Tongli; his wife was née Li. He placed sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Ruzhou, registered in a salt-producing household in Chongde County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Jiqing, he ranked second in birth order, and he was thirty-one, born on the sixth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather was Mengxiong, his father was Fu, and his mother was née Qian. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Rujing and Rulin, and his younger brothers were Ruli, Ruyan, Ruxun, and Ruxing; his wife was née Chen. He placed eighty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Ruolin, registered in a military household in Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zicai, he ranked first in birth order, and he was thirty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Fengyi, a county school Instructor posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Government Service and Left Vice Supervisor of Instruction in the Left Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy; his grandfather was Duanming, Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate; his father was Han, an Imperial University student admitted through annual tribute; and his mother was née Lu. His parents and a grandparent or grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Ruoshu, a tribute scholar, Ruozhi, Ruomao, Ruoke, and Ruomei; his wife was née Weng. He placed twenty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Weng Xiang, registered in a military household in Qiantang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and belonging to the Hangzhou Right Guard, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Changqing, he ranked third in birth order, and he was forty, born on the twenty-third day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, his grandfather was Maochun, his father was Hao, and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cheng and Chun, and his younger brothers were Jia and Su; his wife was née Sun. translation_en:
Tang Chen, registered in an officer household of Daxing Left Guard and a native of Tianchang County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhijing, he ranked first in his family, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Jie, and his father Xiang; his father's former wife was née Wei and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living, and his wife was née Ren; he placed ninety-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jixian, registered in a civilian household in Luzhou, Sichuan, was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Boxiao, he ranked first in his family, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xun, posthumously appointed Prefectural Judge, his grandfather Fuchu, a Subprefect, and his father Song; his mother was née He, and only his mother was living; his elder brothers were Jideng, Jisheng, and Jichang, his younger brothers Jixian and Jixue, and his wife née Wu; he placed sixteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Mu, registered in an artisan household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Shunbin, he ranked sixth in his family, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shangwen, his grandfather Ti, and his father Lin, who held an honorary official title for longevity; his mother was née Zhong, and only his father was living; his elder brothers were Ji, Zhi, and He, and his wife was née Xu; he placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shijian, registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Benjie, he ranked fourth in his family, and he was aged forty-two, born on the twenty-first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongdao, his grandfather Ji, and his father Jin; his father's former wife was née Huang and his mother née Su; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Shiyang, Shiwen, Shitong, Shiliang, and Shigong, his younger brothers Shizhan, Shirang, Shida, and Shixian, and his wife née Zhang; he placed fifty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Shaoru, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shikong; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-three sui old, born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sixian; his grandfather, Gong, was an Assistant Instructor, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his father, Ao, held a nonfunctional rank of the eighth grade; and his mother was née Tang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shaoshi, Shaoli, Tao, Huo, Wei, Shangzhi, Shaowen (a tribute student), and Shaowu; his younger brothers were Shaoyi, He, Zhun, Shaoqian, and Shaoyou. His wife was née Guan. He placed fifty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Huan, registered in Dingzhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenfu; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-one sui old, born on the ninth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Lun, was a Prefect; his grandfather, Xuan, held an honorary official title for public beneficence; his father was Yong; his mother was née Wang; and his stepmother was née Zhou. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zhu, Si, Huang, and Xiang. His wife was née Wang, and his subsequent wife was née Luo. He placed eighty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Mengyang, registered in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a military household and was an supplementary student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shaoming; he ranked first in birth order and was twenty-one sui old, born on the seventh day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Man, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father was Shiru; and his mother was née Huo. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Wu'an and Wubin. He was betrothed to a woman née You. He placed sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qian Qin, registered in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Maowen; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-eight sui old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shi; his grandfather, Da, was posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Qi, was a Prefect; and his mother, née Wang, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability (yiren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xianyue, Xiancen, Fan, Lan, Shen (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Hui; his younger brothers were Wei (a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites), Xuan (a tribute student), Kui (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Rui. His wife was née Fei. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

His courtesy name was Bozhan; he ranked fourteenth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged forty-three, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng; his grandfather, Xian, was a Subprefectural Judge; and his father, Sijing, was a District Magistrate. His mother was née Lü, and his stepmother was née Li; his father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Jing, Lun (District Vice Magistrate), Gang (District Magistrate), Ji, Shou, and Shao; his younger brothers were Jin, Ji, and Yan. His wife was née Lü. He placed forty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chong 李寵, registered in Jingyang County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Rucheng; he ranked fourth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged forty-one, and was born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather was Mei, and his father was Zhen; his mother was née Meng. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His elder brothers were Cai, Chen, and Xiao, and his younger brother was Bin. His wife was née Xiao. He placed first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Pian 戴楩, registered in Mianchi County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Rucai; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was aged forty, and was born on the sixteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yan, was a District Magistrate; his grandfather, Ying, was an Imperial University student; and his father was Gan. His mother was née Bi. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Xie. He placed sixty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Jiugao 黃九臯, registered in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruming; he ranked eleventh among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the nineteenth day of the intercalary fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather was Yuan, and his father, Yi, was an Assistant Prefect; his mother was née Ding. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jiushao, and his younger brothers were Jiuchuan, Jiubao, and Jiushan. His wife was née Zhou. He placed sixty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Quan, registered in Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Wenkui, he ranked fifth in birth order, and he was twenty-six, born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanrui; his grandfather, Bin, was granted the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Cui, and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ke, E, and Duo; his younger brothers were Yue, Zhao, Gao, Xi, Yi, Tang, Kai, and Zhen. His wife was née Zhou. He placed seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhi, registered in Gushi County, Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zishou, he ranked third in birth order, and he was thirty, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deshan, his grandfather was Ying, his father was Zheng, and his mother was née Xu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Fu and Lu. His wife was née Tian. He placed forty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tang, registered in Changsha County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student at the county government school, specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shusi, he ranked second in birth order, and he was twenty-five, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather was Yuancong, his father was Zhongsheng, his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother was née Tao. His father was deceased, and he served his surviving mother. His elder brother was Xiang. His wife was née Peng. He placed twelfth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiamo, registered in Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhongchen, he ranked fourth in birth order, and he was twenty-seven, born on the fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lu, his grandfather was Qi, his father was Zi, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cunren, Cunyi, and Jiayan. His wife was née Fu. He placed third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Youru, registered in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zizhen; he ranked third in his family and was twenty years old, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather was 𤏸 [pronunciation uncertain], an honorary official honored for longevity; his father was Jing, and his mother was née Xu. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Youren, Youlun, and Youqiao; his younger brothers were Youjia, Youxin, Youyi, and Yousi. He married a woman née Dong. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shichun, registered in Guang Prefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Yiyuan; he ranked first in his family and was thirty years old, born on the eighteenth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Kui; his grandfather was Zhi; his father was Wenzhang, and his mother was née Ji. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shixiao; his younger brothers were Shixian, Shiyang, Shixin, and Shiheng. He married a woman née Liu. He placed fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Jianbang, registered in Ba Subprefecture, Baoning Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weixin; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Liang, a Garrison Administrative Clerk; his grandfather was Fengyi, an honorary official honored for longevity; his father was Mo, an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jianzi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Lian, registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziqing; he ranked seventh in his family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Peng, an honorary official honored for public benefactions; his grandfather was Shou, an honorary official honored for longevity; his father was Yingzhen, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his mother was née Wu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Hong, Jiang, Hu, Hai, Yuan, Chao, and 𣶬 [pronunciation uncertain]; his younger brothers were Che, Chun, Xun (a metropolitan graduate, jinshi), Qia, Qu, Mu [?], Han, Song, Xiang, Huai, Ying, Ji, and Pan. He married a woman née Shen. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

裴紳〔貫山西平陽府蒲州軍籍，國子生，治書經，字子書，行二，年二十六，六月初六日生〕。曾祖贊，祖英〔壽官〕，父鼒，母張氏。具慶下，弟綬、純，娶陳氏。山西鄉試第三十五名，會試第一百五十九名。
translation_en:
Third Class: 222 candidates, granted the status of associate metropolitan graduate (tong jinshi chushen).

Liu Xun 劉洵 was registered in a military household in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Ruifu, and he ranked sixtieth in his family’s birth order. He was thirty years old, born on the twelfth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather, Lie, was Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master of Central Rectitude and Vice Director for Aid in Governance; his grandfather, Cheng, was Right Vice Censor-in-Chief in the Censorate, posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Thorough Counsel. His father, Lu, was a Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his mother, née Zhao, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Repose. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Mi, Fa, Zhan, Zhi, Yong, Chong, Zhi 沚, and Jun. He married a woman née Dai. He placed fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yuanchong 張元冲 was registered in a civilian household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shuqian, and he ranked thirty-third in his family’s birth order. He was thirty-seven years old, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather, Yunhui, was honorifically appointed Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs; his grandfather, Yihong, was Left Administration Assistant Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His father, Jingqi, was a Prefect; his mother, née Tang, was granted the title Lady of Respect. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yuanchu, Yuanben, Yuanpu, a Vice Commander in a Wardens’ Office, Yuanjie, and Yuanliang; his younger brothers were Yuanxu, Yuanwan, and Yuanzhong. He married a woman née Hu. He placed eighty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pei Shen 裴紳 was registered in a military household in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zishu, and he ranked second in his family’s birth order. He was twenty-six years old, born on the sixth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zan; his grandfather, Ying, held an honorary office for longevity. His father was Zi, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shou and Chun. He married a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jiang Kun, registered in a civilian household in Yugan County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zipeng; he ranked twenty-eighth in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Tingjie, his grandfather Li, his father Chaozong, and his mother née Yu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jing and Lin, and his younger brothers Huang and Kuai. He married a woman née Shu. He placed second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Guangzhe, registered in a military household in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an annual tribute student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he ranked fifth in his family and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Hua, his grandfather Lin, his father Jing, and his mother née Wang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Guangqi, and his younger brothers Guanghu, Guangzhi, Guangshao, Guangtai, Guangzu, and Guangzhou. He married a woman née Yu. He placed thirteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Yu, registered in a civilian household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an additional-quota student at the prefectural school, specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenshi; he ranked second in his family and was aged twenty-eight, born on the ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ruoshan, his grandfather Zhengyi, his father Shimao, and his mother née Gong. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jing, and his younger brothers Xie and Yan. He married a woman née Wan. He placed eighty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jingxian, registered in a civilian household in Meizhou, Sichuan, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mianzhi; he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-six, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Puzhong, posthumously appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Yuyan, a Prefect; his father was Hongyong, a tribute scholar (gongshi); and his mother was née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Xiangxian. He married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Guo. He placed sixty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Lun, courtesy name Deyan, was registered in an official household in Huai’an Guard under the Wanquan Regional Military Commission and was a native of Yingshang County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Hong and grandfather You were both Battalion Judges; his father was Jin. His father’s former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Han. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shen, Ji, and Wei, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan 𨮐 [given-name reading uncertain], courtesy name Xixing, was registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Siwen was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Minister of War; his grandfather was Ji, and his father was Qi. His mother was née Dai, and his stepmother was née Hu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yu, a tribute scholar, Liao, and Tang; his younger brother was Jin. His wife was née Dai, and his subsequent wife was née Hu. He placed fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Huai, courtesy name Dongzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An Instructor at the Puzhou departmental school in Shandong, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ranked fifth among his brothers, and was aged thirty-seven, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ye was a provincial graduate who served as Acting Instructor at a county school; his grandfather Xiang was a Station Master, and his father was 𨦣 [name reading uncertain]. His mother was née Lin, and his stepmother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Guan, and his wife was née Wu. He placed thirty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Rujin, courtesy name Zixiu, was registered in a civilian household in Luanzhou, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An added student at the departmental school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ao, his grandfather was Youliang, and his father was Jian. His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhang and Rucheng, and his wife was née Xue. He placed ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Tinggao, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was an attached student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruqin. He ranked twenty-first in family order, was twenty-nine years old, and was born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Tan; his grandfather was Lian, posthumously appointed Director in the Ministry of Rites; and his father was Hong. His father's former wife was née Hu, and his mother was née Fan. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Tingjie, Tingxun, Tingzhao, Tingyan, and Tingyi (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort); his younger brothers were Tingqian, Tingrang, and Tingshi. He married a woman née Gui. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Liang, registered in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Kangmeng. He ranked first in family order, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Hong, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; his grandfather was Xiao; his father was Zuan, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Luo. Both parents survived. His younger brothers were Zhi, Tai, and Wen. He married a woman née Cheng and subsequently a woman née Ma. He placed twenty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Song, registered in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, belonged to an artisan household and was a student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruqiao. He ranked first in family order, was twenty-five years old, and was born on the second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather was Jie; his father was Chen; and his mother was née Wei. He had surviving grandparents and parents. His younger brothers were Mei, Chun, Yu, and Zhen. He married a woman née Cai. He placed fifty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Dong, registered in Luxi County, Chenzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student at the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Longzhong. He ranked first in family order, was thirty-six years old, and was born on the ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Mao; his grandfather was Shimian, who held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his father was Tinghe; and his mother was née Yang. He had surviving grandparents and parents. His elder brother was Le, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; his younger brothers were Zhu, Wu, Bai, Jia, and Shu. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed tenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

王士翹〔貫江西吉安府永新縣，民籍，安福縣人，縣學增廣生，治春秋，字民瞻，行一，年三十八，四月十三日生〕。曾祖猷允，祖槐兆，父寛，母劉氏，繼母朱氏。嚴侍下，兄敏〔官生〕、士俊〔府知事〕，弟士翺，娶劉氏，繼娶劉氏。江西鄉試第三十五名，會試第二百八十七名。

顏嘉會〔貫湖廣長沙府攸縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字子亨，行二，年二十五，正月二十一日生〕。曾祖夔〔知縣〕，祖選〔衛經歷〕，父守忠〔知縣〕，母鍾氏。重慶下，兄嘉賓〔監生〕，弟嘉善、嘉慶、嘉兆，娶沈氏。湖廣鄉試第五十一名，會試第一百五十二名。
translation_en:
Feng Xuan, courtesy name Tiqian, was registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the eighteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather, Zhi, was a provincial graduate (juren) who served as acting Assistant Instructor; his father, Pu, held an honorary title for longevity; and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Chao and Bing, and his younger brothers were Mo, Ran, and Xu. His wife was née Ji. He placed fifty-fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Zhizhong, courtesy name Ruyi, was registered in a civilian household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai, his grandfather Kun, his father Luan, and his mother née Gu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Yunzhong, and his younger brothers were Shizhong, Bingzhong, Qizhong, Maozhong, Sizhong, and Yongzhong. He was betrothed to a woman née Xu and married a woman née Zhou. He placed seventy-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shiqiao, courtesy name Minzhan, was registered in a civilian household in Yongxin County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a native of Anfu County. An additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youyun, his grandfather Huaizhao, his father Kuan, his mother née Liu, and his stepmother née Zhu. His father alone of his parents was living. His elder brothers were Min, a student admitted by virtue of an official’s privilege, and Shijun, a prefectural Clerk; his younger brother was Shi’ao. His first wife was née Liu, and he subsequently married another woman née Liu. He placed thirty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Jiahui, courtesy name Ziheng, was registered in a civilian household in You County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, Kui, was a District Magistrate; his grandfather, Xuan, was a Guard Registrar; his father, Shouzhong, was a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Zhong. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother, Jiabin, was a student of the National University, and his younger brothers were Jiashan, Jiaqing, and Jiazhao. His wife was née Shen. He placed fifty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Yin, registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingshu; he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Qian, his grandfather Kui, his father Chu, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zan and Xun, and his younger brothers Liang and Jian. He married a woman née Song. He placed forty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bao Long, registered in a civilian household in Changzhi County, Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shihua; he was fifth in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Duo, his grandfather Zhikui, and his father Cai; his father’s former wife and his mother were both née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ming, Fan (Director of Meals), Ping, and Gong. He married a woman née Qin. He placed thirtieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 302nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Shanglun, registered in an official household attached to the Ceremonial Guard Office of Junzhou, Henan, was a native of Teng County, Shandong, and a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongyi; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fourteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Tong, his grandfather Xing, his father Zong (a Ceremonial Guard in the Ceremonial Guard Office), and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shangjing, and his younger brothers were Shangchun (Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue) and Shangjiong. He married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Kang. He placed second in the Henan Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yi, registered in an artisan household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruheng; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the third day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yongchu, his grandfather Congli, his father Tingqi, and his mother née Fang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Zuosheng. He married a woman née Luo and subsequently a woman née Hu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

薛尚義〔貫直隸河間府河間縣，民籍，府學生，治詩經，字仲行，行二，年三十二，二月二十一日生〕。曾祖景春，祖勝，父隆，母鞏氏。具慶下，兄尚仁，弟尚禮、尚智，娶張氏。順天府鄉試第三十三名，會試第六十六名。

林萬潮〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字養晦，行二，年二十九，正月二十四日生〕。曾祖彌宣〔訓導，封順天府推官，贈兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史〕，祖良〔大理寺評事，贈兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史〕，父富〔兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史〕，前母黃氏〔贈淑人〕，母翁氏〔封孺人，贈淑人〕，生母方氏。具慶下，兄萬仞〔官生〕，弟繼祉、萬載、萬峰、萬殊、繼藩、萬言，娶鄭氏。福建鄉試第二十八名，會試第二百十五名。

陳宗夔〔貫湖廣武昌府通山縣，軍籍，國子生，治易經，字惟一，行一，年三十二，三月初二日生〕。曾祖原甫〔壽官〕，祖琉〔監生〕，父興賢〔訓導〕，母吳氏。重慶下，弟宗蕃，娶宋氏。湖廣鄉試第四十六名，會試第二百九十名。

步允遷〔貫順天府薊州，軍籍，山東高苑縣人，州學生，治禮記，字子安，行一，年二十四，八月初五日生〕。曾祖瀛，祖雄，父天衢〔貢士〕，母李氏。具慶下，娶孟氏。順天府鄉試第九十八名，會試第一百六十二名。
translation_en:
Xue Shangyi, registered in Hejian County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhongxing, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Jingchun, his grandfather Sheng, his father Long, and his mother Lady Gong; both parents were living. His elder brother was Shangren and his younger brothers Shangli and Shangzhi; he married Lady Zhang. He placed thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Wanchao, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Yanghui, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather Mixuan was an Assistant Instructor, honorifically appointed Prefectural Judge of Shuntian Prefecture and posthumously granted the titles of Right Vice Minister of War and concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-chief; his grandfather Liang was a Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, posthumously granted the titles of Right Vice Minister of War and concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-chief; and his father Fu was Right Vice Minister of War and concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-chief. His father's former wife, Lady Huang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Virtue (shuren); his mother Lady Weng was granted the title Lady of Service (ruren) and posthumously the title Lady of Virtue; his birth mother was Lady Fang. Both parents were recorded as living. His elder brother Wanren was a student admitted by virtue of official family status; his younger brothers were Jizhi, Wanzai, Wanfeng, Wanshu, Jifan, and Wanyan. He married Lady Zheng and placed twenty-eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and two hundred fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zongkui, registered in Tongshan County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Weiyi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the second day of the third month. His great-grandfather Yuanfu held an honorary official title granted for longevity, his grandfather Liu was an Imperial University student, his father Xingxian was an Assistant Instructor, and his mother was Lady Wu; his parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Zongfan, and he married Lady Song. He placed forty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bu Yunqian, registered in Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a military household and was a native of Gaoyuan County, Shandong; he was a subprefectural government school student specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Zi'an, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-four, born on the fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Xiong, his father Tianqu, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his mother Lady Li; both parents were living. He married Lady Meng and placed ninety-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

卜大同〔貫浙江嘉興府秀水縣，匠籍，國子生，治書經，字吉夫，行一，年三十，六月二十日生〕。曾祖顒，祖周〔義官〕，父宗洛〔監生〕，前母周氏，母賀氏。具慶下，弟大有、大觀、大順，娶周氏。順天府鄉試第七十名，會試第一百二名。

賈大亨〔貫浙江紹興府上虞縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字貞甫，行三，年四十，九月十二日生〕。曾祖章〔國子監典簿〕，祖暹〔教諭〕，父幼安，母陳氏。具慶下，兄大川，弟大節，娶羅氏。浙江鄉試第五十八名，會試第二百十六名。
translation_en:
Yang Yicheng, registered in Yichun County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Mingfu; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the fifteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Donghui, his grandfather Bingji, his father Chunmei, and his mother née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yijing, Yizheng, Yishen, Yiqian, Yirang, Yijian, Yiliang, Yizhi, Yiqi, and Yiping. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed forty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ao Zongqing, registered in the Shuidejiang Native Chief's Office, Sinan Prefecture, Guizhou, belonged to a civilian household and was originally from Xinyu County, Jiangxi. He was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rucheng; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xuqin, his grandfather Lizhen, and his father Yuanyou; his father's former wife was née Jian, and his mother was née Dong. His mother alone survived. His younger brothers were Guoqing and Jiaqing. He married a woman née Tian and subsequently a woman née Luo. He placed fiftieth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bu Datong, registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jifu; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Zhou, an honorary official, and his father Zongluo, a student of the Imperial University; his father's former wife was née Zhou, and his mother was née He. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dayou, Daguan, and Dashun. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed seventieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Daheng, registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhenfu; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged forty, and was born on the twelfth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhang, Registrar of the Directorate of Education; his grandfather was Xian, an Instructor; his father was You'an, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Dachuan and his younger brother Dajie. He married a woman née Luo. He placed fifty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Rudong, registered in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Bolong. He ranked first in birth order, was twenty-nine years old, and was born on the thirteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Ying, his father Xuan, and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ruliang, Runan (a tribute scholar), and Rucai. He married a woman née Chen. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Yi, registered in Taiping County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shunzhi. He ranked sixteenth in birth order, was thirty-four years old, and was born on the seventeenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Defu, his grandfather Quan, his father Benxiu, and his mother née Liu. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Bian and Ke. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Cheng. He placed ninety-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 133rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Zhengxue, registered in Qianwei County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an added student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zichong. He ranked third in birth order, was thirty-five years old, and was born on the tenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Tianlu, his father Shizhi, and his mother née Jiang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhengxiu, Zhengji (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Zhengyan; his younger brother was Zhengxin. He married a woman née Liu. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Jie was registered in an officer household in the Daxing Left Guard and was a native of Yongqing County, Zhili. He was an added student of the Shuntian prefectural school and specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Erzhan. He ranked first in birth order, was twenty-six years old, and was born on the second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather Qin was a Guard Commander posthumously granted the title General of Manifest Valor; his grandfather Shen was a Guard Commander granted the same title; his father Zhen was a Guard Commander, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ji and Zi [?]. He married a woman née Guo. He placed sixty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Zhu 黃注 was registered in a military household in Xinfeng County, Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Rulin and ranked seventh among his brothers and male cousins; he was thirty-four years old and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ding; his grandfather, Xue, held an honorary official title for public benefaction; his father, Shui, was an annual tribute student; and his mother was née Gan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xun and Qi, and his younger brothers were Bian, Liu, and Zhu. His wife was née Lin. He placed twenty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 207th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Jiuze 楊九澤 was registered in a civilian household in Huayin County, Hua Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zide and ranked first among his brothers and male cousins; he was forty years old and was born on the ninth day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Hui, was a provincial graduate (juren) who served as acting Instructor; his grandfather, Shen, held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his father was Jinzhong; his mother was née Liu; and his stepmothers were née Wang and née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jiuyuan, Jiugong, Jiuchou, Jiujing, Jiuwei, Jiushan, Jiuguan, and Jiushao. His wife was née Liu; his subsequent wives were née Wang and née Liang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tingyi 劉廷儀 was registered under the Imperial Medical Office and was a native of Cixi County, Zhejiang. A Shuntian prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Ruxiu and ranked twentieth among his brothers and male cousins; he was twenty-seven years old and was born on the twenty-third day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Jing, his father Fan, and his mother née Shao. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Tinggao, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort, Tingzhi, Tingyong, and Tingyin. His wife was née Feng. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Huang 張煌 was registered in a civilian household in Huai’an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a native of Min County. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Yongtao and ranked third among his brothers and male cousins; he was thirty-six years old and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was 𨱆 [name reading uncertain]; his grandfather was Yuan, his father Bing, and his mother née Dong. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Xuan, and his wife was née Lin. He placed sixty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Bian, courtesy name Bojing, was registered in a civilian household in Taicang Department, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was listed as first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian, an honorary official for righteousness; his grandfather was Bi, a holder of a seventh-rank prestige title; his father was Yuanxi, a prefectural clerk; and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ru and Han, both students of the Directorate of Education; Lian, a departmental clerk; Tong, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and Chun. His younger brothers were Can; Han (瀚), an annual tribute student; Yuan; Huai; and Shen. He married a woman née Cao. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xicheng, courtesy name Zongyi, was registered in a military household in Lanyang County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was listed as first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, a department magistrate; his grandfather was Jin, an assistant instructor; his father was Jun, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Mao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xihan and Xi’ou. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Han. He placed thirteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Shulian, courtesy name Mingfa, was registered in a military household in Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi. A county government student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was listed as eighth in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the twenty-second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dongche; his grandfather was Kuanjue; his father was Shendao; and his mother was née Ao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shuling and Shufang, and his younger brother was Shu’ai. He married a woman née Xiao and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed thirty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhichen, courtesy name Yuanxiao, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was listed as first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twentieth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng. His grandfather, Chong, was an assistant instructor and received the honorary title of surveillance commissioner. His father, Dong, was a right assistant administration commissioner, advanced to the prestige title of Grand Master Ranked at Court (chaolie dafu). His mother, née Zhao, received the title of Lady of Suitability (yiren). His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Xuewen, Qin, Zhimin, Xueru, and Zhiqing; his younger brothers were Zhibin and Zhihu. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 315th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Hongshi 孫宏軾 was registered in a civilian household in Zi County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yizhan; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, his grandfather Dakui, and his father Qin; his father's principal wife was née Ling, and his mother was née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Honggui and Hongxuan, and his younger brother was Hongzhe. He married a woman née Tang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 320th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tan Qi 譚棨 was registered in a civilian household in Fu Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, and was a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chaoqi; he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benfang, his grandfather Zongxue (an honorary official recognized for public benefactions), and his father Ziwei; his mother was née Shen. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Hai (County Vice Magistrate) and Dong (a ceremonial attendant, shengji guan); his younger brothers were Rong, Tang, Jiang, and Nie. He married a woman née Huang. He placed fifty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yingji 林應箕 was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and was an added-quota student of the prefectural school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Huinan; he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twelfth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ruliang (a seventh-rank prestige official), his grandfather Yong (an honorary official honored for longevity, posthumously appointed Left Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review), and his father Jun (Assistant Surveillance Commissioner). His mother, née Zhu, was posthumously granted the title Ruren (Lady); his stepmother, née Gu, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yingbi, and his younger brothers were Yingchen and Yingdou. He married a woman née Wu. He placed thirty-third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zang Shan 臧珊 was registered in a civilian household in Shanyang County, Huai'an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan territory, and came from the jurisdiction of the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zipei; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, his grandfather Yue, and his father Hai (an honorary official honored for longevity); his mother was née Gao, and his stepmother née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Hu, Lin (a student of the Directorate of Education), Lian, Yuan, Zhu (a student of the Directorate of Education), Ji, and Xuan. He married a woman née Xu. He placed 120th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 276th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Han Yiyou, courtesy name Rubi, was registered in a civilian household in Qingcheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked second in his family and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather, Xiang, and father, Qi, were county magistrates. His father's principal wife was née Jiao, and his birth mother was née Ma. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Yizuo; his younger brothers were Yidong and Yijing. His wife was née Li. He placed fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yangzhi, courtesy name Jingfu, was registered in a civilian household in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather, Zhining, was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather, Jue, was a prefect; and his father, Shi, was an assistant prefect. His mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother was née Huang. His mother was deceased, and he attended his surviving father. His elder brothers were Yangmeng and Yangshi, the latter a battalion commander; his younger brothers were Yangmin and Yangxing. He married a woman née Fu and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Shiyu, courtesy name Weimin, was registered in a military household in Jingzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Decai; his grandfather, Ning, held an honorary official title for longevity; and his father, Jide, was a county magistrate. His father's principal wife was née Sun, and his birth mother was née Pang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Shitong, and his younger brother was Shixuan. His wife was née Wang. He placed ninety-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tingsong, courtesy name Maozhen, was registered in a civilian household in Ansu County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second in his family and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was De; his grandfather was Ming; his father, Zheng, was a county vice magistrate; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tinggui, an assistant prefect, and Tinghuai; his younger brothers were Tingwu and Tingmei. His wife was née Wang. He placed 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhuge Xian, registered in a military household in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shujing; he ranked 136th in his family’s birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yantan; his grandfather was Zongyi, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions; his father was Lang, and his mother was née Fan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shan and his younger brother Hu. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Lin, registered in a military household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zizhen; he ranked fourth in his family’s birth order and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongcong, his grandfather Zheng, and his father Yingxiang; his mother was née He. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Long and Jian. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Xie. He placed eleventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Chong, registered in a civilian household in Dexing County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Junqing; he ranked nineteenth in his family’s birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dan, posthumously granted the title of District Magistrate; his grandfather was Jun, a Department Magistrate; his father was Dun, an honorary official recognized for public benefactions; and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were An and Shou; his younger brothers were Ning, Cheng, Cha, Ji, Yu, Huan, Cai, Mi, Ji, Shen, Wu, and Yan. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed seventy-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Weiyue, registered in an official household in Qingjian County, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zifu; he ranked second in his family’s birth order and was forty-one years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shangjiong, granted the title of Prefect; his grandfather was Yong, Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission, promoted to the prestige titles Zhongfeng Dafu and Zhengzhi Qing; his father was Jie, formerly Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. His legal mother was née Yang, granted the title of Lady of Respect, and his birth mother was née Zhou. His parents were deceased. His elder brother Weizhen and younger brother Weiyu were students of the Directorate of Education; his younger brother Weichi was an Assistant Commander. He married a woman née Liang. He placed fifteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Shi, registered in a civilian household in Guangzhou, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the department school specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhongfu; he ranked second in birth order, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kegong, his grandfather Pilie, and his father Xuan, an Imperial University student. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Xia. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Zhi. He married a woman née Hao and subsequently a woman née Zhao. He placed sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Shouzhen, registered in a civilian household in Jiangdu County, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Ziyi; he ranked second in birth order, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanhe, his grandfather Bin, and his father Xuan, an Imperial University student; his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shouyu and his younger brother Shouyue. He married a woman née Kong and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Xixue, registered in a civilian household in Guangshan County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was an added-quota government student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Bozhi; he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-seven, and was born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xu, his grandfather Ming, an annual tribute student, and his father Zhengben; his mother was née Hu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Ximeng, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Xizeng, Xiyan, Xida, and Xiyi. He married a woman née Lü. He placed thirty-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gu Wen, registered in a military household in Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was an attached student of the department school specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zicheng; he ranked first in birth order, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Zongru, and his father Dun; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Que. He married a woman née Hu. He placed thirty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Chunfu, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xuemu; he ranked first in family order and was thirty-three years old, born on the fifth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Qi, his grandfather He, and his father Hu; his mother was née Lin and his stepmother née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiufu, Yangfu, Kefu, and Defu; his younger brothers were Sanfu, Sufu, Chufu, and Lifu. His wife was née Li. He placed thirty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiong, registered in an official household in Qingping Guard, Guizhou, was a native of Sheng County, Zhejiang, and a student of the guard school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Youming; he ranked seventh in family order and was twenty-four years old, born on the second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Ju was Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, posthumously granted the titles General Who Guards the State and Vice Regional Military Commissioner. His grandfather Zhang was a District Magistrate, granted the honorary title Investigating Censor; his father Mu was Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His mother, née Sun, was granted the title Lady (ruren). Grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Chengzu, a Guard Commander, Xuezu, and Nianzu; his younger brothers were Yao, Lian, and Lang. His wife was née Jin. He placed fifth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Qiao, registered in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shinan; he ranked first in family order and was thirty-four years old, born on the nineteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Yin, and his father Luan; his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji and Dong; his younger brothers were Ke, Jia, He, Gao, Zhi, Bang, and Mu. His wife was née Jia. He placed forty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Kongyang, registered in Wuyi County, Ji Subprefecture, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zizhu; he ranked third in family order and was twenty-nine years old, born on the second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Nai, and his father Haoshi, a student of the Directorate of Education awaiting selection for office; his mother was née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Kongjia, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Konghou; his younger brother was Kongshi. His wife was née Teng. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Zhaowen, registered in Nankang County, Nan’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household. An additional student of the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Rujian; he ranked fifth in birth order and was twenty years old, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Xun, his grandfather Enze, and his father Xiang, an annual tribute student; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhaoxun and Zhaoli, and his younger brother was Zhaowu. He married a woman née Tian. He placed thirtieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Cheng, registered in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bangwei; he ranked first in birth order and was forty years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ding, a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue at Nanjing; his grandfather was Zhang, an honorary official recognized for longevity; and his father was Pei, an Assistant Instructor. His mother was née Li. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed eleventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Weizhong, registered in the Guangning Left Guard, Liaodong, belonged to a military household and was a native of Linqu County, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruwei; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather was Zhen, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director acting as Director in the Ministry of Revenue at Nanjing; and his father was Yu, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His mother, née Fu, had been granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Weijian, a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Weimin, also a tribute scholar, Weine, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year, and Weizhi. He married a woman née Jiang. He placed twenty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Yue, registered in Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xinfu; he ranked second in birth order and was thirty-eight years old, born on the third day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Sizhong, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Ying, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Gou, a prestige official of the seventh rank, and his younger brother was Lu, a student of the Directorate of Education. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Pang. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.
