translation_en:
Wang Guozhen, courtesy name Yining, was registered in a civilian household in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A classical scholar specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked twenty-second among his male siblings and cousins, was aged twenty-six, and was born on the seventeenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yande, his grandfather Yudai, his father Kai, and his mother née Mao; both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Guochen, and his younger brothers were Guoyan, Guobin, Guowang, and Guoqi. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed twenty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tianchong, courtesy name Zicheng, was registered in a military household in Mengjin County, Henan Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Duan, his grandfather Feng, his father Ying, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Tianding. He married a woman née Meng. He placed twenty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Sanwei, courtesy name Shaoqin, was registered in a military household in Changle County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather Zhen was an Assistant Magistrate of a subprefecture; his grandfather was Xian, and his father Shihong was also an Assistant Magistrate of a subprefecture. His mother was née Zhao and his stepmother née Zhang; his father was living, but his mother was deceased. His younger brothers were Sanjin and Sanshan. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed thirtieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Wenxi, courtesy name Gongjue, was registered in a civilian household in Lianjiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Tai, his grandfather Shi, his father Yuan, and his mother née Qiu; both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Wengang. He married a woman née Su. He placed twenty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zheng Yiluan, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Mingyang; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty-seven, and was born on the eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yongkuan, his grandfather Guan, his father Hu, and his mother née Cai. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Yifeng, and his wife was née Feng. He placed seventy-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Jin, registered in Yichun County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yizhi; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Qiyuan, his grandfather Ai, his father Luan, and his mother née Tang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Qian, Dao, Yuan, Di, Xun, Yu, and Xuan; his wife was née Zhang. He placed fifty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Chengqian, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan territory, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Jiangyin County. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Deguang; he ranked third among his brothers, was aged forty-two, and was born on the fifth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Menghu, his grandfather Shi, his father Pin, and his mother née Gu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Song, a prefectural registrar, Nan, and Zhen; his younger brothers were Cheng, Kai, and Ge. His wife was née Xiao. He placed twenty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Shangwen, registered in Xincheng County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan territory, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhiqing; he ranked first among his brothers, was aged forty-three, and was born on the eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Haiquan, and his father Da, a tribute scholar (gongshi). His father's former wives were née Qi and née Cui; his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Bowen, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed 106th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Zonglu 蔣宗魯, courtesy name Daofu, was registered in a military household in Pu'an Guard, Guizhou, and was a native of Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture. An additional student at the Pu'an Subprefectural School specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-two years old, born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Ming; his grandfather was Sheng, an honorary official for charitable service; and his father was Tingbi, a student at the Nanjing Directorate of Education. His father's former wives were née Xu and née Wang, and his mother was née Luo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qin and Zongzhou, and his younger brother was Zongzeng. His wife was née Pan. He placed fifteenth in the Guizhou Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Hefang 李和芳, courtesy name Renfu, was registered in a military household in Gong'an County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An attached student at the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Qian; his grandfather was Deming, an eighth-rank prestige official; and his father was Xiu, a student of the Directorate of Education. His mother was née Yan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Wenfang, a tribute scholar, and his younger brothers were Yuanfang, Xifang, and Qunfang. His wife was née Cao. He placed forty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Zheng 朱徵, courtesy name Jinqing, was registered in a civilian household in Tang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wenchang; his grandfather was Kuan; and his father was Feng. His mother was née Liu, and his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was De, and his wife was née Yang. He placed eightieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zonggai 黃宗槩, courtesy name Shijie, was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student at the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked ninth among his brothers and was thirty-three years old, born on the sixteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather was Houqing; and his father was Jikui. His mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shang, Zongqi, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, Zongzhi, Zongkan 宗侃, and Zongkan 宗偘. His first wife was née Lin, and his subsequent wife was née Zhang. He placed fifty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qi Zongdao, registered in a military household of Guangning Right Guard in Liaodong and originating from Rizhao County, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shulu; he ranked thirty-second in family birth order and was aged thirty, born on the twelfth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was San, his grandfather Bin, and his father You, a Registrar; his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chun and Zongxian, the latter a Battalion Commander; his younger brothers were Tai, Zongrui, and Zongzhe. He married a woman née Geng. He placed fifty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dao, registered in an official household of Hengzhou Guard, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yunzhong; he ranked thirty-second in family birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Jue, a Battalion Commander, and his father Xian; his mother was née Lu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Ben, an Assistant Commander, and Li; his younger brother was Xuan. He married a woman née Fan. He placed seventy-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Shou, registered in a commoner household of Shuangliu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Weiyi; he ranked first in family birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanhe, his grandfather Zhi, and his father Bing, an Assistant Prefect; his mother was née Wang and his stepmother née Shi. He had living parents and at least one living grandparent. His younger brothers were Ke and Zhi. He married a woman née Ren. He placed fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Shen, registered in an artisan household of Le'an County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Boshu; he ranked third in family birth order and was aged thirty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Cong, and his father Yu, a County Assistant Magistrate; his mother was née Zhu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Ji, a Prefectural School Instructor, Lun, and Jin; his younger brothers were Zeng and Shou. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Cui. He placed forty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lin Mian 林冕, courtesy name Duanwu, was registered in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a civilian household. He was an added student of the county Confucian school and specialized in the Book of Odes. Second in birth order, he was thirty years old and was born on the twenty-first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Di; his grandfather, Tai; his father, Xiu; and his mother, née He. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Chang 㫤 and Hao; his younger brothers were Sheng 昇, Sheng 晟, and Gao. He married a woman née Guo. He placed fifty-ninth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Rui 張瑞, courtesy name Yingshi, was registered in Hui’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. He was an annual tribute student and specialized in the Book of Odes. First in birth order, he was forty years old and was born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongyuan; his grandfather, Rongke; his father, Kun; and his mother, née Sun. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Qi. He married a woman née Huang. He placed forty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Miao Wenlong 繆文龍, courtesy name Weide, was registered in Wusa Guard, Guizhou, in a military household, and was originally from Huating County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Book of Documents. Third in birth order, he was twenty-nine years old and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai; his grandfather, Ren; his father, Liangyu, a district magistrate; and his mother, née Xie. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wenxian and Wenying; his younger brothers were Wenming and Wenshu. He married a woman née Qian. He placed thirty-eighth in the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ge Tingzhang 葛廷章, courtesy name Chaoxian, was registered in an artisan household under the Gongzheng Office in Lanzhou, Lintao Prefecture, Shaanxi. He was a student of the subprefectural Confucian school and specialized in the Book of Documents. Second in birth order, he was thirty-five years old and was born on the twenty-second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather, Zhong; his father, Lin; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Tingmei. He married a woman née Mi and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed thirtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Lingyun 李凌雲 was registered in Junzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Zipeng and was third in birth order, aged twenty-six, born on the seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather, Quan; and his father, Yan, who was granted the title of Investigating Censor. His mother, née Zhou, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chengyun, an Investigating Censor, and Dengyun, a Right Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; his younger brothers were Piyun, Wangyun, Qingyun, and Canyun. His wife was née Shi. He ranked tenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Guangpu 鄭光溥 was registered in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Bogong and was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather, Tang; and his father, Xi, a Court Usher. His mother was née Yu. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Ma. He ranked first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xueyi 劉學易 was registered in Shouguang County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Daofu and was fourth in birth order, aged forty-one, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Wengui; his grandfather, Sen; and his father, Yun, a County Magistrate. His mother was née You. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His wife was née Wang. He ranked ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Heng 趙恒 was registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household. An added student in the prefectural Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Zhizhen and was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Sen, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Huan, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father was Xin. His mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Chen. His wife was née Wang. He ranked fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

朱家相，貫河南開封府歸德州民籍，直隸太倉州人，國子生，治詩經，字伯鄰，行二，年二十九，十一月二十二日生。曾祖純，祖洪，父壽，母錢氏。慈侍下。兄卿，弟宰。娶范氏。河南鄉試第七十九名，會試第二百九十九名。

黃洪毗，貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，府學生，治書經，字協恭，行二，年三十二，八月十六日生。曾祖玉英〔贈南京翰林院侍講學士奉直大夫〕，祖瀾〔南京翰林院侍講學士〕，父肯堂〔貢士〕，母張氏。慈侍下。兄洪崑，弟洪鵬、洪翰、洪化。娶陳氏。福建鄉試第二十二名，會試第四十四名。

translation_en:
Li Shan, courtesy name Jingfu, was registered in an official household of Hengzhou Guard, Huguang, and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked first in birth order, and was aged thirty-four, born on the second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yun; his grandfather was Xian, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was En; and his mother was née Wang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Long, Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; Kui, Guard Commander; Feng; Han; and Qi (琦). His younger brothers were Qiang, Ji, Zhu, and Suo. His wife was née Wang. He placed seventy-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Jiaxiang, courtesy name Bolin, was registered in a civilian household in Guide Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and was originally from Taicang Subprefecture in Zhili. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked second in birth order and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather was Hong; his father was Shou; and his mother was née Qian. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Qing, and his younger brother was Zai. His wife was née Fan. He placed seventy-ninth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Hongpi, courtesy name Xiegong, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked second in birth order, and was aged thirty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yuying, posthumously granted the titles of Expositor-in-waiting of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy and Grand Master for Upright Service; his grandfather was Lan, Expositor-in-waiting of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy; his father was Kentang, a tribute scholar; and his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Hongkun, and his younger brothers were Hongpeng, Honghan, and Honghua. His wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Ning, courtesy name Yanjing, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes, ranked seventh in birth order, and was aged forty-six, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Bo; his grandfather was Fu; his father was Zhu; and his mother was née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan, Left Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; Kuan; and Yin. His younger brothers were Mi, an official awaiting selection for appointment; Rui, a County Magistrate; and Wan. His wife was née Lin. He placed thirty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Jing, registered in Cizhou, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). His courtesy name was Bochang; he ranked third in his family and was thirty-nine years old, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Ying, his grandfather Zhongyou, his father Guang, and his mother née Ke. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Fu and Xian, and his younger brothers Biao, Jin, and Lun. He married a woman née Li. He placed fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Ce, registered in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes (Shijing). His courtesy name was Zhifu; he ranked third in his family and was thirty years old, born on the ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Puxuan, his grandfather Hong, his father Quan, and his mother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xun and Cai, and his younger brother Hui. He married a woman née Qiu. He placed eleventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 308th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Meng, registered in Chuzhou in the Metropolitan Region, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes (Yijing). His courtesy name was Duanfu; he ranked fifth in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was He; his grandfather Yungong was a prefectural school instructor; and his father Xu was a prefectural judge, honorifically invested as a secretary in the Ministry of Rites and posthumously honored as a prefect. His father's former wife, née Wang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Respect; his mother, née Li, was granted the title Grand Lady of Respect. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Ying, an assistant commander; Xiao, a director of food service; Zi, an honorary official; Cun, a surveillance vice commissioner; and Ji. His younger brothers were Hou and Fu. He married a woman née Fang. He placed 133rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yonghe, registered in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural government school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes (Shijing). His courtesy name was Yuanle; he ranked first in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the tenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Jun, his grandfather Zhan, his father Jian, and his mother née Han. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yongjing, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Yongzhong. He married a woman née Su. He placed twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳相〔貫直隸順德府內丘縣民籍，縣學生，治書經，字汝立，行一，年二十五，八月十六日生〕。曾祖參，祖真，父聰，嫡母張氏，生母吕氏。慈侍下，娶龔氏。順天府鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百九十一名。

楊梁〔貫浙江衢州府西安縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字廷材，行七，年二十八，正月十一日生〕。曾祖昊〔推官〕，祖錞〔歲貢生〕，父澍，母葉氏。具慶下，兄棠，弟棐，娶鄭氏。浙江鄉試第十二名，會試第二百二十四名。

劉起宗〔貫四川重慶府巴縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字宗之，行一，年三十五，八月初四日生〕。曾祖規〔監察御史，贈光祿大夫、柱國、少傅兼太子太傅、禮部尚書、文淵閣大學士〕，祖春〔掌詹事府事，資政大夫、禮部尚書兼翰林院學士，贈太子太保，謚文簡〕，父彭年〔按察司按察使〕，母牟氏〔封恭人〕。具慶下，弟起元、起東〔監生〕、起溟、起蒙、起敬、起莘、起江，娶李氏，繼娶柳氏。四川鄉試第二名，會試第一百五名。
translation_en:
Dai Weishi, registered in a salt-producing household in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Bingwen; he ranked sixty-eighth in family birth order, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongru; his grandfather, Minju; his father, Guang, a prefectural Assistant Prefect; and his mother, née Gao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Weizhong and Weixiao, and his younger brothers were Weizong, Weizheng, and Weiji. He married a woman née Huang. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Xiang, registered in a civilian household in Neiqiu County, Shunde Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruli; he ranked first in family birth order, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the sixteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Can; his grandfather, Zhen; and his father, Cong. His father's principal wife was née Zhang, and his birth mother was née Lü. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. He married a woman née Gong. He placed forty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Liang, registered in a civilian household in Xi'an County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingcai; he ranked seventh in family birth order, was aged twenty-eight, and was born on the eleventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Hao, a Judge; his grandfather, Chun, an annual tribute student; his father, Shu; and his mother, née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tang, and his younger brother was Fei. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Qizong, registered in a civilian household in Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongzhi; he ranked first in family birth order, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Gui, an Investigating Censor, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Preceptor concurrently serving as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion. His grandfather was Chun, who directed the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent and held the titles Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Rites concurrently serving as Academician of the Hanlin Academy; he was posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the name Wenjian. His father was Pengnian, a Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and his mother was née Mou, invested with the title Lady of Respect. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qiyuan, Qidong (an Imperial University student), Qiming, Qimeng, Qijing, Qishen, and Qijiang. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Sicheng, courtesy name Zixiu, was registered in a civilian household in Gu’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was originally from Chang’an County, Shaanxi. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather, Gan; and his father, Yong. His father’s former wife was Lady Zhang, and his mother was Lady Xin. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Sijing and Siming; his younger brothers were Simao, Sirui, and Siyuan. He married Lady Sun and subsequently Lady Tong. He placed thirtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Yu, courtesy name Fanzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xi, a provincial graduate (juren) who served as acting Instructor; his grandfather was Zhang; his father, Yuanzhi; and his mother, Lady Lin. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Kan, Che, Shu, and Qu. He married Lady Chen. He placed eighty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Huai, courtesy name Yuchuan, was registered in a civilian household in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. An attached student of the prefectural school specializing in the Record of Rites, he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the seventeenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Xi; his father, Tinglan, a Steward; and his mother, Lady Xie. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ze, Jin, and Zhu. He married Lady Tian and subsequently Lady Su. He placed nineteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Xi, courtesy name Tinghe, was registered in a civilian household in Yongding County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin; his grandfather, Shao; his father, Shihong; and his mother, Lady Zheng. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Kan, a Medical Instructor, and his younger brother was Jun. He married Lady Lai. He placed ninety-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Bao Daoming, registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); his courtesy name was Xingzhi, he ranked eighth in family order, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Wensu, his father Rongfang, and his mother née Wang; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Qing, Lun, Lian, Guang, Shou, Ji, and Long, and his younger brothers Chun, Shen, Qiu, Jian, Xiang, Mai, Da, Yuan, and Xuan; his wife was née Fang; he placed fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Yuchun, registered in a civilian household in Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, and a native of Changshu County, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites (Liji); his courtesy name was Tiren, he ranked fourth in family order, was aged forty-one, and was born on the twenty-second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Huan (posthumously granted the title of District Magistrate), his grandfather Yong, his father Chong, and his mother née Lu; his parents and grandparents were deceased; his elder brothers were Fuchun, Maochun, and Shouchun, and his younger brothers Fangchun, Cuichun, and Fuchun; his wife was née Wang; he placed thirty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Dawu, registered in a civilian household in Jiangling County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes (Yijing); his courtesy name was Xiangcheng, he ranked first in family order, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the thirtieth day of the intercalary first month. His great-grandfather was Sui, his grandfather Yongning, his father Peng, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Daben, Dazhang, and Dahe; his first wife was née Xu, and his subsequent wife née Wang; he placed fifteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cheng Shisi, registered in a military household in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes (Yijing); his courtesy name was Yixue, he ranked twenty-fourth in family order, was aged twenty-five, and was born on the seventeenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Wanyuan, his grandfather Fuchang, his father Ta (㒓), his mother née Wang, and his stepmother née Wu; both parents were living; his elder brother was Shiming, and his younger brothers Shixiang, Shixing, Shimao, Shiji, Shizhang, Shishi, and Shishi (時軾); his wife was née Zheng; he placed sixty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Dong Zice, registered in a military household in Hefei County, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a native of Jingshan County, Huguang. He was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yuanzheng. He ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the twelfth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather was Zhong, an honorary official recognized for longevity; his father was Yue; and his mother was née Chen. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Liu. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Zhao was registered in a military household in Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi. He was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yiming. He ranked seventh among his brothers and was twenty-three years old, born on the nineteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sichu; his grandfather was Jingfa; his father was Shigai; and his mother was née He. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Rujing, Ruliang, Ruyi, and Ruwen. He married a woman née Gu. He placed forty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Chunze was registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. He was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Renfu. He ranked eighth among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather was Wei, a prefectural school instructor; his father was Bi; and his mother was née Sheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Xiu. He married a woman née Lin. He placed seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yuanxiang was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. He was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Guozhong. He ranked fourth among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boyi; his grandfather was Chun; his father was Long; and his mother was née Xue. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yuanji, Yuanqing, and Yuanzhen; his younger brothers were Yuanli, a student of the Imperial University, Yuankang, Yuanlu, and Yuande. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and three hundred ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Nie Li 聶櫟, registered in a military household of Linqing Guard, Shandong, was originally from Xiangfu County, Henan. A student of the Jining Subprefectural School specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Gongshou, ranked second among his brothers, and was twenty-seven years old, born on the eleventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rang; his grandfather, Zheng, was an Assistant Instructor; his father, Zan, was a stipendiary government student; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chu and his younger brother Sheng. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Shi. He placed twenty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Luosheng 劉洛生 was registered in a civilian household in En County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Xicheng, ranked second among his brothers, and was twenty-three years old, born on the nineteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather, Jin, held the honorary designation of Official for Righteousness; and his father, Gao, was a County Registrar. His father's former wives were née Ma and née Guo, and his mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brother, Lusheng, was an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Guansheng, Minsheng, and Yansheng. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Dashi 劉大實, registered in a civilian household in Queshan County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was originally from Zichuan County, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Zixu, ranked first among his brothers, and was twenty-four years old, born on the twelfth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Jian, his father Fu, and his mother née Dong. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Dazhen and Daguan. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Hu 陳鵠, registered in an official household of Shaoxing Guard, Zhejiang, was originally from Wujin County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Mingxiao, ranked second among his brothers, and was thirty years old, born on the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Jie, his grandfather, Yi, and his father, Rui, each held the office of Company Commander. His mother, née Li, was granted the title Lady of Peace. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother, He, was a Company Commander; his younger brothers were Ming, Feng, and Wu. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Zhu. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Binghu, courtesy name Guozhen, was registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mian, an Imperial University student; his grandfather was Daoheng, a prestige official of the seventh rank; and his father was Chaosheng, a county magistrate. His father's principal wife was née Weng, and his birth mother was née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Bingyi, Bingchun, Yingfeng, and Daji; his younger brothers were Bingchen, Bingqian, and Bingchu. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed fourteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wenqing, courtesy name Zhifu, was registered in a military household in Sanyuan County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the sixteenth day of the intercalary first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weixiao; his grandfather was Tong; his father was Zhicong; and his mother was née Shi. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Qinqing and Siqing. He married a woman née Du. He placed first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Chuanji, courtesy name Juqing, was registered in an artisan household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the nineteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongying; his grandfather was Zhenci; his father was Yan; his mother was née Cheng; and his stepmother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuanheng, Zaijia, and Jiming; his younger brothers were Bing'e, Pengzhuo, and Wanxing. He married a woman née Chen. He placed twenty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Fengming, courtesy name Zishi, was registered in a military household of Chenzhou Guard, Huguang, and was a native of Xuyi County, Zhili. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, a company commander; his grandfather was Li; his father was Jing; and his mother was née Yan. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Fengyi. He married a woman née Gao. He placed fortieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

歐陽建〔貫廣東廣州府新會縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字參可，行一，年三十九，二月十三日生〕。曾祖乾禎，祖暾〔義官〕，父純熙，母伍氏。具慶下，弟律、津，娶陳氏。廣東鄉試第二十六名，會試第二百七十二名。
translation_en:
Wu Lan, registered in a civilian household in Huoshan County, Liu'an Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a native of Zhanyi Subprefecture, Yunnan, and a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Qingpei. He ranked first in his family and was forty-four years old, born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Tai, was a prefectural school instructor; his father, Fengyi, was an assistant instructor; and his mother was née Yan. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Chai, and his wife was née Li. He placed 107th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 318th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Bin, registered in a civilian household in Teng County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a native of Qinghe County in the directly administered metropolitan region and a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Dabin. He ranked first in his family and was twenty-eight years old, born on the sixteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was You; his grandfather, Ming; his father, Shu; his mother, née Niu; and his stepmother, née Zou. His father and stepmother were living. His younger brother was Ru, and his wife was née Sun. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Liangfu was registered in a civilian household in Dongxiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a prefectural government school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Zibi. He ranked twenty-third in his family and was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lu; his grandfather, Cheng, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father, Ji, was an assistant instructor; and his mother was née Yue. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Liangqi, and his wife was née Deng. He placed eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang Jian was registered in a civilian household in Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Canke. He ranked first in his family and was thirty-nine years old, born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qianzhen; his grandfather, Tun, held an honorary official title for philanthropy; his father was Chunxi, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lü and Jin, and his wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
洪庭桂〔貫福建泉州府南安縣軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字德馨，行三，年三十五，九月二十日生〕。曾祖敏倫，祖昕〔義官〕，父宙，母林氏，繼母吳氏。嚴侍下，兄庭芳、庭梧、庭實〔貢士〕，弟庭秀、庭蘭，娶余氏。福建鄉試第七十一名，會試第六十一名。

胡堯臣〔貫四川重慶府安居縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯純，行二，年三十二，正月二十五日生〕。曾祖存禄，祖鵬，父自明〔訓導〕，母朱氏。重慶下，兄誠，弟舜臣、禹臣，娶楊氏。四川鄉試第五十名，會試第一百四名。

董懋中〔貫直隸保定府安州高陽縣人，國子生，治書經，字德甫，行二，年二十三，九月二十四日生〕。曾祖榮，祖紋，父兵，母王氏。具慶下，兄用中、執中〔貢士〕、希中〔貢士〕、秉中、化中，弟常中、協中、正中、龍中、虛中、啓中、適中，娶苑氏。順天府鄉試第二十六名，會試第二百二十四名。

郭惟清〔貫武功中衛匠籍，直隸崑山縣人，順天府學附學生，治書經，字寅仲，行一，年三十，十月初二日生〕。曾祖福敬，祖泰，父昇，母楊氏。具慶下，弟惟和、惟一，娶文氏。順天府鄉試第一百六名，會試第二百二十八名。
translation_en:
Hong Tinggui, courtesy name Dexin, was registered in a military household in Nan’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twentieth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Minlun; his grandfather, Xin, held the honorary designation “Official for Righteous Conduct”; his father was Zhou; his mother was née Lin, and his stepmother née Wu. His father was living, his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Tingfang, Tingwu, and Tingshi (a tribute student); his younger brothers were Tingxiu and Tinglan. His wife was née Yu. He placed seventy-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Yaochen, courtesy name Bochun, was registered in a military household in Anju County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cunlu; his grandfather was Peng; his father, Ziming, was an Assistant Instructor; and his mother was née Zhu. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Cheng; his younger brothers were Shunchen and Yuchen. His wife was née Yang. He placed fiftieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Maozhong, courtesy name Defu, was from Gaoyang County, Anzhou Subprefecture, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-three, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather was Wen; his father was Bing; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yongzhong, Zhizhong (a tribute student), Xizhong (a tribute student), Bingzhong, and Huazhong; his younger brothers were Changzhong, Xiezhong, Zhengzhong, Longzhong, Xuzhong, Qizhong, and Shizhong. His wife was née Yuan. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Weiqing, courtesy name Yinzhong, was registered in an artisan household under the Wugong Central Guard and was a native of Kunshan County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An attached student of the Shuntian prefectural government school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fujing; his grandfather was Tai; his father was Sheng; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Weihe and Weiyi. His wife was née Wen. He placed 106th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

倪瑗〔貫陝西咸寧縣民籍，直隸長洲縣人，府學生，治春秋，字公引，行四，年三十五，十一月初八日生〕。曾祖曙，祖顥〔散官〕，父通〔封給事中〕，嫡母劉氏〔封孺人〕，生母劉氏。慈侍下，兄璣〔按察司僉事〕、環〔驛丞〕、玳〔貢士〕、瑶、珮，弟璜〔監生〕，娶黃氏。陝西鄉試第五十六名，會試第一百四十六名。

translation_en:
Ni Yuan 倪瑗, registered in a civilian household in Xianning County, Shaanxi, and a native of Changzhou County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Gongyin; he ranked fourth in his family and was thirty-five years old, born on the eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shu; his grandfather, Hao, held a prestige title; and his father, Tong, was granted the title of Supervising Secretary. His father's principal wife, née Liu, was granted the title of Lady (ruren); his birth mother was also née Liu. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Ji, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; Huan, Station Master; Dai, a tribute scholar; Yao; and Pei. His younger brother Huang was an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Huang. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Gun 袁衮, registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Buzhi; he ranked third in his family and was forty years old, born on the sixteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cong; his grandfather, Jing; his father, Ding, a Battalion Commander; and his mother, née Han. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Biao, Vice Commander in a Nanjing Police and Fire Office, and Ji. His younger brothers were Bao, an Imperial University student; Mao, a sacrificial official in the household of the Prince of Xiang; and Qiu. He married a woman née Lu. He placed sixty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhuang Sikuan 莊思寬, registered in a civilian household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Junli; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-three years old, born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yize; his grandfather, Yuanshan; his father, Long; and his mother, née Guo. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brother was Sigong, and his younger brother was Sixin. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Yan 孟顏, registered in a civilian household in Zezhou, Shanxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xueyan; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-four years old, born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather, Biao, was posthumously granted the title of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, with the additional posthumous title of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather, Chun, held the prestige title of Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and served as Left Vice Minister of Personnel. His father, Yang, was a Messenger, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his mother, née Yan, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Xuekong, Xuesi, Fu, Xu, and Xueyao. He married a woman née Pang. He placed third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
劉乾〔貫直隸保定府唐縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字仲坤，行三，年三十二，千月十一日生〕。曾祖著〔敎諭〕，祖瑜〔翰林院檢討〕，父汝教，母左氏。慈侍下，兄鼎、泰，弟恒，娶王氏，繼娶徐氏。順天府鄉試第一百十七名，會試第二百十九名。

趙之屏〔貫四川順慶府南充縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字憲甫，行二，年二十八，十二月十四日生〕。曾祖永富，祖廷爵，父愷，母師氏。具慶下，弟之翰、之藩、之綱、之紀，娶韓氏。四川鄉試第七名，會試第一百四十五名。

甄成德〔貫山西太原府平定州守禦千戶所軍籍，嵐縣人，國子生，治書經，字行叔，行一，年三十八，七月初四日生〕。曾祖海，祖福祥，父鏞，母郭氏。具慶下，弟成業、成性、成仁、成義，娶馬氏。山西鄉試第三十八名，會試第二百五十一名。

冷珂〔貫四川重慶府榮昌縣軍籍，湖廣麻城縣人，國子生，治易經，字鳴叔，行五，年四十，六月二十日生〕。曾祖廷傑，祖奎〔累贈奉政大夫、府同知〕，父宗元〔知府〕，母張氏〔贈宜人〕，繼母鄭氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下。四川鄉試第五十九名，會試第一百四十名。
translation_en:
Liu Qian, registered in a military household in Tang County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhongkun; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the eleventh day of the month transcribed as 千 [?]. His great-grandfather was Zhu, a Confucian School Instructor; his grandfather was Yu, an Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy; his father was Rujiao, and his mother was née Zuo. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Ding and Tai, and his younger brother was Heng. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Xu. He ranked 117th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Zhiping, registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xianfu; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Yongfu, his grandfather was Tingjue, his father was Kai, and his mother was née Shi. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhihan, Zhifan, Zhigang, and Zhiji. He married a woman née Han. He ranked seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhen Chengde, registered in a military household of the Pingding Subprefecture Guard Battalion, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, and a native of Lan County, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Xingshu; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hai, his grandfather was Fuxiang, his father was Yong, and his mother was née Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chengye, Chengxing, Chengren, and Chengyi. He married a woman née Ma. He ranked 38th in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Leng Ke, registered in a military household in Rongchang County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, and a native of Macheng County, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Mingshu; he was fifth in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Tingjie; his grandfather was Kui, who received successive posthumous grants of the titles Grand Master for Governance and Prefectural Vice Prefect; his father was Zongyuan, a Prefect. His mother, née Zhang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother, née Zheng, was granted the same title. His father and stepmother were both living. He ranked 59th in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

孟廷相〔貫順天府霸州，軍籍，州學生，治《書經》，字爰立，行一，年三十五，十一月十二日生〕。曾祖安〔府照磨〕，祖欽〔七品散官〕，父瑛〔州學正〕，母胡氏。具慶下，弟廷芳、廷鄰，娶司氏。順天府鄉試第二十八名，會試第二百四十五名。

劉選〔貫河南汝寧府汝陽縣，民籍，山西安邑縣人，府學生，治《詩經》，字子銓，行一，年二十八，八月十六日生〕。曾祖順，祖江，父亮，嫡母王氏，生母張氏。具慶下，娶鄭氏。河南鄉試第二名，會試第一百九名。

王尚學〔貫廣西柳州府馬平縣，民籍，縣學生，治《易經》，字敏叔，行四，年三十，四月十一日生〕。曾祖昕，祖沂，父相，母文氏。具慶下，娶陳氏。廣西鄉試第三名，會試第二百三名。

王德〔貫浙江温州府永嘉縣，軍竈籍，縣學附學生，治《詩經》，字汝脩，行三，年二十一，閏十二月十二日生〕。曾祖廷芳，祖蠲，父浥，母林氏。具慶下，兄慶、立，娶邵氏。浙江鄉試第八十名，會試第七十三名。
translation_en:
Meng Tingxiang, courtesy name Yuanli, was registered in Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture, in a military household. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twelfth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was An, a prefectural Records Examiner; his grandfather was Qin, an official with seventh-rank prestige title; his father was Ying, a subprefectural school Instructor; and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tingfang and Tinglin, and his wife was née Si. He placed twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 245th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Xuan, courtesy name Ziquan, was registered in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household, and was originally from Anyi County, Shanxi. A student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the sixteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Shun, his grandfather Jiang, and his father Liang; his legal mother was née Wang and his birth mother née Zhang. His parents were living. His wife was née Zheng. He placed second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shangxue, courtesy name Minshu, was registered in Maping County, Liuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the eleventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Yi, his father Xiang, and his mother née Wen. Both parents were living. His wife was née Chen. He placed third in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang De, courtesy name Ruxiu, was registered in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a military salt-producing household. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-one, and born on the twelfth day of the intercalary twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Tingfang, his grandfather Juan, his father Yi, and his mother née Lin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qing and Li, and his wife was née Shao. He placed eightieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

謝體升，貫江西吉安府吉水縣，軍籍，縣學生，治易經，字順之，行五，年三十三，三月二十五日生。曾祖建康，祖克選〔義官〕，父顯簪〔義官〕，前母高氏，母蕭氏，繼母周氏。具慶下，兄體蒙〔監生〕、體師、體鼎〔監生〕，弟體復，娶黃氏。江西鄉試第五十一名，會試第二百二十七名。

唐時，貫直隸保定府雄縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字學孔，行一，年二十七，十月二十一日生。曾祖興，祖全，父林，母高氏。具慶下，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十一名，會試第四十一名。

魏謙吉，貫直隸真定府栢鄉縣，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字子惠，行四，年三十，十一月初一日生。曾祖鑑，祖壽〔訓導〕，父巖〔儒官〕，母趙氏。具慶下，兄謙光〔監生〕、謙亨、謙利，弟謙貞、謙榮、謙勞、謙撝，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第二名，會試第五名。

張情，貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣，匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字約之，行二，年三十六，九月二十四日生。曾祖思明，祖繪，父祥〔歲貢生〕，母杜氏。慈侍下，兄性，弟意〔按察司副使〕、心，娶朱氏。應天府鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百二名。
translation_en:
Xie Tisheng, registered in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shunzhi, and he ranked fifth among his brothers. He was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiankang; his grandfather, Kexuan, and father, Xianzan, both held honorary official status for charitable contributions. His father’s former wife was née Gao, his mother née Xiao, and his stepmother née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Timeng (an Imperial University student), Tishi, and Tiding (an Imperial University student); his younger brother was Tifu. His wife was née Huang. He placed fifty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Shi, registered in Xiong County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Xuekong, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Quan, his father Lin, and his mother née Gao. Both parents were living. His wife was née Li. He placed 121st in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wei Qianji, registered in Baixiang County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zihui, and he ranked fourth among his brothers. He was thirty years old, born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Shou, was an Assistant Instructor; his father, Yan, was a Confucian educational official; and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qianguang (an Imperial University student), Qianheng, and Qianli; his younger brothers were Qianzhen, Qianrong, Qianlao, and Qianhui. His wife was née Li. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qing, registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an artisan household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuezhi, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siming, his grandfather Hui, and his father Xiang (an annual tribute student); his mother was née Du. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Xing; his younger brothers were Yi (a Surveillance Vice Commissioner) and Xin. His wife was née Zhu. He placed forty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Tao was registered in a military household of Tianjin Left Guard in Zhili and was a native of Xiangcheng County, Henan. A guard-school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Renfu and ranked third in birth order; he was twenty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xing; his grandfather, Qing; his father, Qi, held an honorary title for longevity; and his mother was née Shi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xun and Chen, and his wife was née Chen. He placed forty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zha Bingyi was registered in a civilian household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Xingfu and ranked eighth in birth order; he was thirty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Shi; his grandfather, Yi, had been honorarily granted the title of Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his father was Hui, and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Bingzhong, Bingzhi, Bingheng, Bingqing, Bingquan, and Bingquan 秉銓, the last a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brothers were Bingyue, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Binglun, Bingxin, Binglü, and Bingjun. His wife was née Lu. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shiliang was registered in a civilian household in Sui'an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county-school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he had the courtesy name Yuanliang and ranked third in birth order; he was thirty, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ruguang; his grandfather, Shiya, held an honorary title for longevity; his father was Han, and his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shien and Shizhong, and his younger brothers were Shiyi and Zonglu. His wife was née Ling; he subsequently married a woman née Yan. He placed ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Zhao was registered in a civilian household in Jiyang County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A county-school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Chaoxuan and ranked first in birth order; he was twenty-eight, born on the sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Bin; his grandfather, Yu; and his father, Dao. His father's former wife was née Liu, and his mother was née Zhou. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Lü, Chou, Hua, and Ru. His wife was née Xie; he subsequently married another woman née Xie. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qiu Dai 丘玳, courtesy name Wenyu, was registered in a military household in Liu’an Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Song; his grandfather, Xuan; his father, Fu; and his mother, née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Heng, and his younger brother was Rui. He married a woman née Gong and subsequently a woman née Wang. He ranked 109th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shi 李實, courtesy name Youhua, was registered in a civilian household in Lingbao County, Henan Prefecture, Henan. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zi, an honorary official for righteousness; his grandfather, Mengyang; his father, 𦶜 [name reading uncertain]; and his mother, née Ge. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jiyi and Jiru, and his younger brother was Shou. He married a woman née Yan. He ranked 74th in the Henan Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Xuan 許瑄, courtesy name Bowen, was registered in an artisan household in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. An attached student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Shunqian; his grandfather, Chenggao; his father, Yuanming; and his mother, née Zheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Lin, and his younger brother was Huan. He married a woman née Xiao. He ranked 83rd in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qian 張潛, courtesy name Shijian, was registered in an official household in Qihe County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was twelfth in birth order and aged twenty-two [?; the transcription is garbled here], and was born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Chun; his grandfather, Juren, Left Chief Administrator; his father, Jiujing; and his mother, née Bi. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Jin, Dong, Yang, Lai, Xiang, and Zhan. He was betrothed to a woman née Li. He ranked 32nd in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Rugui, courtesy name Dexin, was registered in Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked third in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the twelfth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Shizuo, his grandfather Gao, his father Maozhe, and his mother née Li; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhao, Wen, and Qiao, and his wife was née Ji. He placed eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Shiyan, courtesy name Kejing, was registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked sixth in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the tenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ruming, posthumously granted the title of Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; his grandfather was Qi, an honorary official recognized for public beneficence; his father was Lu; his legal mother was née Ang, and his birth mother née Li. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Shixian, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Shiyong, Shixuan, Shifan, Shida, and Shijian; his younger brothers were Shigao, Shijin, Shizhi, Shirang, and Shishang. He married a woman née Ji and subsequently a woman née Liu. He placed tenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 312th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Tingxiu, courtesy name Gongshang, was registered in Chunhua County, Bin Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked seventh in his family and was aged thirty, born on the eighth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yi, a subprefect; his grandfather was Jiuxiao, an honorary official honored for longevity; his father was Renfu, and his mother née Yuan. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Tingfu, and his wife was née Yao. He placed fifty-second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 307th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Zhi, courtesy name Yunli, was registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, his family rank is recorded as “六十一一” [?]; he was aged thirty-seven, born on the thirteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Ning, his grandfather Qi, his father Mi, a county magistrate, and his mother née Mao; both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shu and Yu, and his wife was née Chen. He placed sixtieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Shanji 余善繼 was registered in a civilian household in Changshou County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Boxian, and he ranked first in birth order. He was twenty-seven, born on the third day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongshou; his grandfather, Zhong, was a Professor in a princely establishment; his father was Long, and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tingchong, and his younger brothers were Nengji and Keji. His wife was née Xie. He placed thirty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 310th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Daonan 吳道南 was registered in a civilian household in Guangzhou, Runing Prefecture, Henan, and was originally from Fengcheng County, Jiangxi. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenzai, and he ranked second in birth order. He was thirty-one, born on the twelfth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shirong; his grandfather was Quan; his father was Zhaofeng; his mother was née Jin, and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Daoming, and his wife was née Cai. He placed fifty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zaiming 楊載鳴 was registered in a scholarly household in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xuqing, and he ranked second in birth order. He was twenty-five, born on the twenty-third day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yu, was Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; his grandfather was Wen; his father, Xun, was an Instructor, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zaifang, and his younger brother was Zaishang. His wife was née Long. He placed fifteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 100th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Lian 沈鍊 was registered in a military household of Shaoxing Guard, Zhejiang, and was originally from Lishui County. He was a student of the Imperial University and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chunfu, and he ranked fifth in birth order. He was thirty-two, born on the eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bocai; his grandfather was Qing; his father was Bi, and his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhen, Kai, and Chuan; his younger brothers were Hao, Zhong, Fu, Yi, and E. His wife was née Xu. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

符驗〔貫浙江台州府黃巖縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字大克，行亨六一作，年四十，六月十四日生〕。曾祖永廉，祖孚，父匡〔教諭〕，母金氏。永感下，兄璽，弟瓊，娶王氏，繼娶吳氏。浙江鄉試第七名，會試第八十八名。

高謙〔貫陝西綏德衛，軍籍，榆林衛人，國子生，治春秋，字孔益，行五，年二十六，七月十八日生〕。曾祖旺，祖冀〔百戶〕，父鸞〔府都事〕，前母王氏，母張氏。慈侍下，兄奎〔百戶〕、儒〔千戶〕、科、第，娶時氏。陝西鄉試第四十六名，會試第二百三十九名。
translation_en:
Li Yihan, registered in Xianju County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yuanfu, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liangping, his grandfather Zhen, his father Guan, and his mother née Peng; both parents were living, his elder brothers were Yiguan, Yijian, and Yichao, his younger brother was Yipei, and his wife was née Ying; he placed eighty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hong En, registered in Huangmei County, Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Congren, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the fourteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuxuan, his grandfather Sheng, a County Magistrate, his father Mo, a Registrar, and his mother née Hu; his parents and grandparents were living, his younger brothers were Xun, Kui, and Zao, and his wife was née Wang; he placed thirty-sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Yan, registered in Huangyan County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Dake, his birth-order entry is garbled (亨六一作) [?], and he was aged forty, born on the fourteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yonglian, his grandfather Fu, his father Kuang, a School Instructor, and his mother née Jin; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Xi, his younger brother was Qiong, and he married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Wu; he placed seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Qian, registered in Suide Guard, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household, was a native of Yulin Guard, and was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Kongyi, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-six, born on the eighteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Ji, a Company Commander, his father Luan, a prefectural Administrative Clerk, his father's former wife née Wang, and his mother née Zhang; his mother was living and his father deceased, his elder brothers were Kui, a Company Commander, Ru, a Battalion Commander, Ke, and Di, and his wife was née Shi; he placed forty-sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.
